31:1: Surah Luqman In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Surat Al-Baqarah discusses in general what is related to the beginning of this surah, which is that God, the Most High, made this Qur’an a guidance, healing and mercy for the doers of good, who are those who do good deeds by following the Shariah, so they establish the obligatory prayers within their limits and times and what follows them of voluntary and non-obligatory prayers, and give the obligatory zakat to those who deserve it, and maintain ties of kinship and relatives, and are certain of the reward in the Hereafter, so they desire the reward from God for that, not to show off with it, nor do they desire a reward from people or thanks. Whoever does that in this way, is among those about whom God, the Most High, says: Those are upon guidance from their Lord, meaning upon insight, evidence and a clear and distinct path, and it is those who are the successful, meaning in this world and the Hereafter.

31:6: When God the Almighty mentioned the state of the happy ones, who are those who are guided by the Book of God and benefit from hearing it, as He the Almighty said: “God has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book, oft-repeated. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it; then their skins and their hearts soften at the remembrance of God” verse, He followed it up by mentioning the state of the wretched ones who turned away from benefiting from hearing the Word of God and turned to listening to flutes and singing with melodies and musical instruments, as Ibn Masoud said about the Almighty’s statement: And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [others] from the way of God verse. He said: By God, it is singing. Ibn Jarir narrated: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Yazid ibn Yunus told me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah al-Bajali, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu al-Sahba’ al-Bakri, that he heard Abdullah ibn Mas’ud being asked about this verse: And of mankind is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [people] from the way of God. Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: Singing, by God, there is no god but Him, repeating it three times. Amr ibn Ali told us: Safwan ibn Isa told us: Hamid al-Kharrat told us, on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu al-Sahba’ that he asked Ibn Mas’ud about the statement of God: And of mankind is he who buys the amusement of speech, he said: Singing. And this is what Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Makhul, Amr ibn Shu’ayb, and Ali ibn Nadima said. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: This verse, And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [people] from the way of God without knowledge, was revealed about singing and musical instruments. Qatada said: His statement, And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [people] from the way of God without knowledge, by God, he might not spend money on it, but buying it is recommended, as it is enough of a person’s misguidance to choose false speech over true speech, and that which is harmful over that which is beneficial. It was said that by his statement, he buys the amusement of speech, he meant buying female singers from among the slave girls. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Khallad al-Saffar, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Zahr, on the authority of Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “It is not permissible to buy or sell female singers, and consuming their price is forbidden. Concerning them, God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘And among mankind is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [people] from the way of God.’” And thus it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Ubaydullah ibn Zahr in a similar manner. Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith, and the aforementioned Ali ibn Yazid is weak. I say Ali, his sheikh, and the one who narrated from him are all weak, and God knows best. Ad-Dahhak said about the verse: {And of mankind is he who buys idle talk} He said: He means polytheism. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said the same. Ibn Jarir preferred that it is any speech that turns people away from the verses of God and following His path. His statement, {to mislead [people] from the path of God} means that he only does this to oppose Islam and its people. And if the ya’ is read with a fat-ha, the lam is the lam of consequence or an explanation of the divine decree, meaning that they were destined to be like this. And the verse: {and takes it in ridicule} Mujahid said: And takes the path of God in ridicule, mocking it. Qatadah said: It means and takes the verses of God in ridicule, and Mujahid’s statement is more appropriate. And His statement, For those is a humiliating punishment, meaning, just as they belittled the verses of God and His path, they will be humiliated on the Day of Resurrection in eternal and ongoing punishment. Then God the Almighty said, And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as if he had not heard them, as if there was deafness in his ears, meaning, this person who is drawn to amusement, play, and entertainment, when the verses of the Qur’an are recited to him turns away from them, turns away, and turns a deaf ear, as if he did not hear them because he is harmed by hearing them, as he has no benefit from them and no interest in them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, which will cause him pain just as he was harmed by hearing the Book of God and His verses.

31:8: This is a mention of the destiny of the righteous among the happy ones in the Hereafter, who believed in God and believed the messengers, and did righteous deeds in accordance with God's law. For them are gardens of pleasure, meaning they will enjoy therein various types of comforts and pleasures, including food, drink, clothing, housing, vehicles, women, freshness, and hearing, which no one has ever imagined. They will remain in that state forever, never moving away, nor seeking to be deprived of it. And the Almighty's saying: The promise of God is true, meaning this will inevitably come to pass because it is from God's promise, and God does not break His promise, because He is the Generous, the Giver of good things, the Doer of whatever He wills, the Able to do all things. And He is the Exalted in Might, who has subdued all things and everything is subject to Him. The Wise, in His words and deeds, who made the Qur'an a guidance for the believers. "Say, 'It is, for those who believe, a guide and a healing. But those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is, upon them, blindness.'" And He said, And We send down from the Qur’an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.

31:10: With this, the Almighty demonstrates His great power to create the heavens and the earth, and everything in them and between them. He the Almighty says: He created the heavens without pillars. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: They have no visible or invisible pillars. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Mujahid said: They have pillars that you do not see. This issue has been explained earlier at the beginning of Surat Ar-Ra’d, so there is no need to repeat it. And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, meaning the mountains anchored the earth and weighed it down so that it would not move with its people on the surface of the water. For this reason, He said: lest it should move with you, meaning lest it should move with you. God the Almighty says: {And He dispersed therein every kind of moving creature} meaning, He dispersed therein every kind of animal, the number of whose shapes and colors is known only to the One Who created them. Since He, the Almighty, has affirmed that He is the Creator, He points out that He is the Provider by saying: {And We sent down water from the sky and caused to grow therein every noble kind} meaning, every kind of plant is noble, that is, beautiful to look at. Al-Sha’bi said: People are also from the plants of the earth, so whoever enters Paradise is noble, and whoever enters Hell is ignoble. God the Almighty says: {This is the creation of God} meaning that what God the Almighty mentioned of the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them came from God’s action, creation, and decree, and He alone has no partner in that. For this reason, God the Almighty says: {Then show me what those other than Him have created} meaning of what you worship and call upon of idols and rivals. {Rather, the wrongdoers} meaning those who associate others with God and worship others besides Him are in manifest error} meaning, ignorance and blindness. {Of course, there is no god but God} meaning, clear and apparent, with no hidden meaning.

31:12: The early Muslims differed about Luqman 31:Was he a prophet or a righteous servant without prophethood? There are two opinions, the majority are on the second. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-Ash'ath from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas who said: Luqman was an Abyssinian slave who was a carpenter. Qatadah narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: I said to Jabir ibn Abdullah: What has reached you about Luqman? He said: He was short and had a flat nose due to his descent. Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab who said: Luqman was from the blacks of Egypt, with long lips. God gave him wisdom and prevented him from prophethood. Al-Awza'i said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah narrated to me that a black man came to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab asking him, so Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said to him: Do not be sad because you are black, for among the best of people were three blacks: Bilal, Mahja', the freed slave of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Luqman the Wise. He was a black Nubian with long lips. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Khalid Al-Rab’i, who said: Luqman was an Ethiopian slave who was a carpenter. His master said to him, Slaughter this sheep for us. So he slaughtered it. He said, Take out the two best parts of it. So he took out the tongue and the heart. Then he waited as long as God willed, then he said, Slaughter this sheep for us. So he slaughtered it. He said, Take out the two worst parts of it. So he took out the tongue and the heart. His master said to him, “I ordered you to take out the two best parts of it, so you took them out. And I ordered you to take out the two worst parts of it, so you took them out?” Luqman said, There is nothing better than these two when they are good, and nothing worse than these two when they are bad. Shu’bah said, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: Luqman was a righteous slave, but he was not a prophet. Al-A'mash said: Mujahid said: Luqman was a black slave with thick lips and cracked feet. Hakam bin Salim said on the authority of Saeed Al-Zubaidi on the authority of Mujahid: Luqman the Wise was an Abyssinian slave with thick lips and cracked feet, and he was a judge over the Children of Israel. Another narrator said that he was a judge over the Children of Israel during the time of David, peace be upon him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Al-Hakam told us, Amr bin Qais told us: Luqman was a black slave with thick lips and cracked feet. A man came to him while he was talking to some people and said to him: Are you not the one who used to tend the sheep with me in such and such a place? He said: Yes. He said: What brought you to this point? He said: Truthfulness and keeping silent about what does not concern me. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Safwan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdur-Rahman bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Jabir, who said: God raised up Luqman the Wise by His wisdom. A man whom he had known before saw him and said to him: Are you not the slave of the Banu So-and-so whom you used to herd their flocks yesterday? He said: Yes. He said: What has brought you to this point? He said: The decree of God, fulfilling trusts, speaking the truth, and leaving what does not concern me. Some of these narrations explicitly deny that he was a prophet, and others imply that, because his being a slave who had been touched by slavery contradicts his being a prophet, because messengers were sent among the lineages of their people. For this reason, the majority of the early Muslims were of the view that he was not a prophet. His being a prophet is only transmitted from Ikrimah, if the chain of transmission to him is sound, because it was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim said, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Luqman was a prophet. This Jabir is Ibn Yazid Al-Ju’fi, and he is weak, and God knows best. Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Abdullah ibn Ayyash al-Qatbani told me on the authority of Umar, the freed slave of Ghafra, who said: A man stood before Luqman the Wise and said: Are you Luqman? Are you a slave of Bani Al-Hashas? He said: Yes. He said: Are you a shepherd of sheep? He said: Yes. He said: Are you the black man? He said: As for my blackness, it is obvious, so what do you like about me? He said: People treading on your carpet, coming to your door, and being pleased with what you say. He said: O son of my brother, if you listen to what I say to you, you will be like that. Luqman said: Lower your gaze, hold your tongue, be chaste in your food, guard your private parts, speak truthfully, fulfill your covenant, honor your guest, protect your neighbor, and leave what does not concern me. That is what has brought me to what you see. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Nufayl told us, Amr ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Abdah ibn Rabah, on the authority of Rabi’ah, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, that he said one day, mentioning Luqman the Wise, and said: He was not given what he was given because of his family, wealth, lineage, or qualities, but he was a quiet, silent man, who pondered for a long time, and had deep insight. He never slept during the day, and no one ever saw him spit or cough, or urinate or defecate, or wash, or play or laugh. He would not repeat a statement he had made unless he said a piece of wisdom that someone would repeat to him. He had married and had children, but they died and he did not cry over them. He would visit the sultan and go to the judges to look, ponder, and consider, and that is why he was given what he was given. A strange narration was reported on the authority of Qatada, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, who said: My father told us, Al-Abbas bin Al-Waleed told us, Zaid bin Yahya bin Ubaid Al-Khuza’i told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Ibn Bashir Qatada, who said: God gave Luqman the Wise the choice between prophethood and wisdom, and he chose wisdom over prophethood. Gabriel came to him while he was sleeping and sprinkled wisdom on him, or he sprinkled wisdom on him. He said: So he woke up speaking with it. Saeed said: I heard Qatada say: Luqman was asked: How did you choose wisdom over prophethood, when your Lord gave you the choice? He said: If He had sent me a firm resolve to prophethood, I would have hoped to achieve success from Him, and I would have hoped to carry it out, but He gave me the choice, and I feared that I would be too weak to prophethood, so wisdom was dearer to me. This is from the narration of Saeed bin Bashir, and it contains a weakness that they have spoken about because of it, and God knows best. What Saeed bin Abi Aruba narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding the Almighty’s statement: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom, meaning understanding of Islam, and he was not a prophet and revelation was not sent to him. And His statement, And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom, meaning understanding, knowledge and expression, to be grateful to God, meaning We commanded him to thank God Almighty for what God had given him, bestowed upon him and granted him of the grace with which He had singled him out from among his kind and the people of his time. Then God the Almighty said, And whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself, meaning the benefit and reward of that only return to the grateful, as God the Almighty said, And whoever does righteousness - it is for themselves that they prepare. And His statement, “And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is Free of need of His servants, and will not be harmed by that, even if all the people of the earth disbelieved, for He is Free of need of anyone other than Him. There is no god but God, and we worship none but Him.
31:13: God the Almighty says, informing us about Luqman's advice to his son, who is Luqman bin Anqa' bin Sadun, and his son's name is Tharan, according to a statement narrated by Al-Suhayli. God the Almighty mentioned him in the best way, and that He gave him wisdom. He is advising his son, who is the most compassionate and beloved of people to him, so he deserves to be given the best he knows, and for this reason He first advised him to worship God and not associate anything with Him. Then He warned him, Indeed, associating others with Him is a great injustice, meaning it is the greatest injustice. Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: When the verse, Those who have believed and have not mixed their belief with injustice, was revealed, this was difficult for the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and they said: Who among us has not mixed his faith with injustice? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “That is not the case. Have you not heard the words of Luqman, ‘O my son, do not associate anything with God. Indeed, association is a great injustice.’” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-A’mash with it. Then he coupled his command to him to worship God alone with being kind to his parents, as God the Almighty said, And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment. God the Almighty often couples this in the Qur’an, and here He said, “And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents: his mother carried him, with hardship upon hardship.” Mujahid said, The hardship and weakness of the child. Qatadah said, Exertion upon effort. Ata’ Al-Khurasani said, Weakness upon weakness. And His statement, And his weaning is in two years, meaning his upbringing and breastfeeding after his birth is in two years, as God Almighty said: Mothers shall breastfeed their children two complete years for whoever desires to complete the nursing (al-An’am 2:17). From here Ibn Abbas and other imams deduced that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, because He said in the other verse, And his gestation and weaning is thirty months. 31:16: These are beneficial commandments that God the Almighty has narrated from Luqman the Wise, for people to comply with and follow. He said, O my son, indeed, if it be the weight of a mustard seed, meaning that even if the injustice or sin were the weight of a mustard seed, some of them allowed the pronoun in his saying it is to be a pronoun for the matter and the story, and on this basis it was allowed to raise weight, but the first is more appropriate. And the Almighty's saying, God will bring it forth, meaning God will bring it forth on the Day of Resurrection when He sets up the just scales, and will reward for it, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil, as God the Almighty said, And We will set up the Balance of Justice for the Day of Resurrection, so not a soul will be wronged at all, the verse. God Almighty said: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. Even if that atom were protected and veiled inside a solid rock, or absent and lost in the regions of the heavens and the earth, God would bring it to light, because nothing is hidden from Him, and not an atom’s weight in the heavens or the earth escapes Him. For this reason God Almighty said: Indeed, God is Kind and Aware. That is, He is Kind in knowledge, so nothing is hidden from Him, no matter how small, delicate, or insignificant they are. Aware of the crawling of an ant in the dark of night. Some of them claimed that what is meant by His statement, and it will be inside a rock, is a rock under the seven earths. Al-Suddi mentioned it with his chain of transmission, which is narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and a group of the Companions, if it is authentic. This is also narrated on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi, Abu Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Minhal bin Amr, and others. This - and God knows best - seems to have been received from the Israelite stories, which are neither truthful nor false. What appears - and God knows best - is that what is meant is that if this seed, despite its insignificance, were it to be inside a rock, God would reveal it and make it manifest with His subtle knowledge. As Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, If one of you were to work inside a solid rock that had no door or window, his work would be revealed to the people, whatever it may be. Then he said, O my son, establish prayer, meaning within its limits, obligations, and times. And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, meaning according to your ability and effort. And be patient over what befalls you. He knew that the one who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong will inevitably be harmed by the people, so He commanded him to be patient. His statement, Indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of resolve, means that patience in the face of people’s harm is for the one who has resolve. His statement, And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people, means do not turn your face away from people when you speak to them or they speak to you out of contempt for them and arrogance towards them. Rather, be gentle and smile at them, as it came in the hadith, Even if you meet your brother with your face beaming toward him, beware of letting your lower garment trail, for it is from conceit, and God does not like conceit. Ali ibn Abi Talha said that Ibn Abbas spoke about the verse, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning, do not be arrogant, thus belittling God's servants, and turn your face away from them when they speak to you. Al-Awfi and Ikrimah narrated this same verse from him. Malik said that Zaid ibn Aslam said, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning, do not speak while turning away. This was also narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Yazid ibn al-Asam, Abu al-Jawza', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and others. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said, He means speaking with a frown. The first statement is correct. Ibn Jarir said, "The root of sa'r is a disease that afflicts camels in their necks or heads, until their necks are torn away from their heads, so it is used to describe an arrogant man. This is the origin of the statement of Amr ibn Hayyi al-Taghlabi." And when the tyrant turned his cheek, we rose up to face him from his sway. Abu Talib said in his poetry: In the past, we did not accept injustice. If they bent their heads, we would correct them. His statement, And do not walk upon the earth exultantly, meaning arrogantly, haughtily, and stubbornly. Do not do that, and God will hate you. That is why He said, Indeed, God does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful, meaning one who is arrogant and conceited, proud of himself or others. And God the Almighty said, "And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height." We have already discussed this in its proper place. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami told us, Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Abi Laila told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who said: Arrogance was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he emphasized it, saying, God does not love any arrogant boaster. A man from among the people said, By God, O Messenger of God, when I wash my clothes, I like their whiteness, and I like the strap of my sandals and the strap of my whip. He said, “That is not arrogance. Arrogance is to belittle the truth and look down on people.” And he narrated it from another chain of transmission in a similar manner, and in it is a long story, and the killing of Thabit and his will after his death. His saying, And be moderate in your walk, means walk moderately, neither slow and hesitant, nor excessively fast, but rather walk in a moderate manner. His saying, And lower your voice, means do not exaggerate in your speech and do not raise your voice over anything that is useless. For this reason, he said, The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys. Mujahid and others said: The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys, meaning that the ultimate goal of raising one’s voice is that it resembles donkeys in its loudness and height, and despite this, it is hateful to God Almighty. This likening of donkeys in this case requires that it be forbidden and strongly condemned, because the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, “There is no evil example for us: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit.” Al-Nasa’i said in his interpretation of this verse: Qutaybah ibn Sa’id told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If you hear the crowing of roosters, then ask God for His bounty. And if you hear the braying of donkeys, then seek refuge in God from Satan, for they have seen Satan.” The rest of the group, except Ibn Majah, narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on his authority. In some versions: at night. And God knows best. These are very beneficial pieces of advice, and they are from the stories of Luqman the Wise from the Qur’an. Many wise sayings and sermons have been narrated from him, so let us mention a model and a constitution for that. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Sufyan told us, Nahshal ibn Majma’ al-Dhabi told me, on the authority of Qaz’ah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) told us, “Verily, Luqman the Wise used to say: ‘When God entrusts something to Him, He protects it.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Musa ibn Sulayman, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Luqman said to his son while admonishing him, ‘O my son, beware of covering your face, for it is frightening at night and reprehensible during the day.’ He said: My father told us, Amr bin Othman told us, on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Al-Tharri bin Yahya, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, wisdom has seated the poor in the company of kings. He also said: My father told us, Abdah bin Sulaiman told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Abdul Rahman Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, when you come to a gathering of people, shoot them with the arrow of Islam, meaning peace, then sit in their corner and do not speak until you see that they have spoken. If they are engrossed in the remembrance of God, then extend your arrow with them, but if they are engrossed in something else, then move on to someone else. He also said: My father told us, Amr bin Saeed bin Katheer bin Dinar told us, Damrah told us on the authority of Hafs bin Omar, who said: Luqman placed a bag of mustard next to him, and he began to admonish his son and take out a mustard seed until the mustard ran out. Then he said: O my son, I have admonished you with an admonition that if a mountain were admonished with it, it would crack. So his son cracked. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn Abd al-Baqi al-Masisi told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Harrani told us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Taraifi told us, Anas ibn Sufyan al-Maqdisi told us, on the authority of Khalifa ibn Salam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Take the blacks as your wives, for three of them are among the leaders of the people of Paradise: Luqman the Wise, the Negus, and Bilal the muezzin.” Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: He meant the Abyssinians. Chapter on idleness and humility This is related to the will of Luqman, peace be upon him, to his son. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya compiled a separate book on this, and we will mention its objectives from it. He said: Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir told us, Abdullah bin Musa Al-Madani told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid bin Hafs bin Abdullah bin Anas, on the authority of his grandfather Anas bin Malik, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, There may be a disheveled man wearing two cloaks who turns away from people’s doors, but when he swears an oath by God, God fulfills his oath. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Ja’far bin Sulayman, on the authority of Thabit, and Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it, and he added, Among them is Al-Bara’ bin Malik. Abu Bakr bin Sahl Al-Tamimi said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Nafi’ bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayyash bin Abbas, on the authority of Isa bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar may God be pleased with him, that he entered the mosque and saw Muadh bin Jabal weeping at the grave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said to him: What makes you weep, Muadh? He said: A hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I heard him say: “A little showing off is polytheism, and God loves the pious, the hidden, the wealthy, who, when absent, are not missed, and when present, are not recognized. Their hearts are lamps of guidance, and they are saved from every dark cloud.” Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ narrated to us, Affan ibn Ali narrated to us, on the authority of Humaid ibn Ata’ al-A’raj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said, “There may be a man of two cloaks who is not paid attention to, if he were to swear by God, He would fulfill his oath. If he were to say, ‘O God, I ask You for Paradise,’ He would give him Paradise and would not give him anything of this world.” He also said, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Among my nation is he who, if he came to the door of one of you and asked Him for a dinar or a dirham or a fils, He would not give it to him. If he asked God for Paradise, He would give it to him. If he asked Him for the world, He would not give it to him, nor would He withhold it from him because of its insignificance to him. He is a man of two cloaks who is not paid attention to, if he were to swear by God, He would fulfill his oath.” This is a mursal hadith from this chain of transmission. He also said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman told us, Awf told us, Abu Hurayrah said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Among the kings of Paradise are those who are disheveled and dusty, wearing two cloaks, and no one pays attention to them. They are those who, when they ask permission to see the rulers, are not given permission, and when they propose marriage to women, they are not married to them, and when they speak, they are not listened to. The needs of each one of them are churning in his chest. If his light were divided among the people on the Day of Resurrection, it would suffice them.” He said: Umar ibn Shabbah recited to me on the authority of Ibn Aishah, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Is there not a man with two cloaks in a house whose carpets are scattered and whose bedspreads are covered with rugs? His rivers flowed around his palace, and his gardens shone and surrounded him. It was also narrated from the hadith of Ubaidullah bin Zahr, from Ali bin Zaid, from Al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God said: ‘The most envied of My friends is a believer who is light-hearted, has a share of prayer, worships his Lord well and obeys Him in secret, and is obscure among the people and is not pointed at with fingers if he is patient in that.’” He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his hand in his pocket and said: His death hastened, his inheritance is small, and those who mourn him are few. And from Abdullah bin Amr, he said: The most beloved of God’s servants to God are the strangers. It was said: Who are the strangers? He said: Those who fled with their religion will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection to Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: I have been told that God the Almighty will say to the servant on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Did I not bestow blessings upon you, did I not give you, did I not cover you? Did I not... did I not... did I not humble your memory? Then Al-Fudayl said: If you can avoid being known, then do so. It does not matter if you are not praised, and it does not matter if you are blamed by people but praised by God. Ibn Muhayriz used to say: O God, I ask You for a humble memory. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad used to say: O God, make me among the highest of Your creation in Your sight, and make me among the lowest of Your creation in my own eyes, and among the people among Your average creation. Chapter on what was said about fame Then he said: Ahmad bin Isa Al-Masry told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Harith and Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Sinan bin Sa’d, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “It is enough for a man to be protected from evil, except for the one whom God has protected, that people point fingers at him in his religion and his worldly life. God does not look at your outward appearance, but at your hearts and your deeds.” And something similar was narrated on the authority of Ishaq bin Al-Bahlol, on the authority of Ibn Abi Fadik, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul-Wahid Al-Akhnasi, on the authority of Abdul-Wahid bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like this. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said to Al-Hasan: You are being pointed at with fingers, so he said: What is meant is the one who is pointed at in his religion with innovation and in his worldly life with immorality. On the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, he said: Do not start to become famous, and do not raise your person to be remembered, and learn but keep quiet, and be silent so that you will be safe, please the righteous and enrage the wicked. Ibrahim bin Adham may God have mercy on him said: He who loves fame has not spoken the truth about God. Ayoub said: No servant has spoken the truth about God except that he would be pleased not to know his place. Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ said: He who loves God loves that people do not know him. Samak bin Salamah said: Beware of having many friends. Abaan bin Othman said: If you want your religion to be safe, then have fewer acquaintances. If more than three people sat with Abu Al-Aaliyah, he would get up and leave them. He said: Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: Talha saw some people walking with him and said: They are flies of greed and moths of Hellfire. Ibn Idris narrated on the authority of Harun ibn Ibn Antara on the authority of Salim ibn Hanzala who said: While we were with my father, Umar ibn al-Khattab struck him with a whip and said: This is a humiliation for the follower and a trial for the followed. Ibn Awn narrated on the authority of al-Hasan: Ibn Masoud went out and some people followed him. He said: By God, if you knew why my door was locked, not two men among you would follow me. Hammad ibn Zayd said: When we passed by a gathering and Ayyub was with us and greeted us, they would respond vehemently, which would upset him. Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar: Ayyub used to make his shirt long, and he was asked about that. He said: Fame in the past was in the length of the shirt, but today it is in rolling it up. He once made sandals similar to those worn by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He wore them for a few days, then took them off and said: I have never seen people wearing them. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: Do not wear clothes that make scholars famous or that make fools look down on you. Al-Thawri said: They disliked fine clothing that would make one famous and in which people would raise their eyes to him, and poor clothing that would make one look despised and humiliate one’s religion. Khalid bin Khidash narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hasana, the companion of Al-Ziyadi, who said: We were with Abu Qilabah when a man wearing cloaks entered upon him. He said: Beware of this braying donkey. Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said: There are people who have placed arrogance in their hearts and humility in their clothing. The one wearing a cloak is greater with his cloak than the one wearing a cloak with his cloak. Why do they miss each other? In some reports, it is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, said to the Children of Israel: Why do you come to me wearing the clothing of monks, while your hearts are the hearts of wolves? Wear the clothing of kings, and soften your hearts with fear. Chapter on good character Abu At-Tayyah said on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was one of the best people in character. And on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Umar: It was said, O Messenger of God, which of the believers is best? He said, The one with the best character. And on the authority of Nuh ibn Abbad on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), “Indeed, a servant may attain, through his good character, the ranks of the Hereafter and the noblest of stations, even though he is weak in worship, and he may attain, through his bad character, the depths of Hellfire, even though he is a worshipper.” And on the authority of Sayyar ibn Harun on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Good character takes away the best of this world and the Hereafter. And on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Indeed, a servant may attain, through his good character, the rank of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts during the day. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Abu Muslim Abd Al-Rahman bin Yunus told me, Abdullah bin Idris told us, my father and uncle told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the thing that most often admits people to Paradise, and he said, Fear of God and good character. And he was asked about the thing that most often admits people to Hell, and he said, “The two hollows: the mouth and the private parts.” Usamah bin Sharik said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Bedouins came to him from every direction and said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?’ He said, ‘Good character.’” Ya'la bin Samak said, on the authority of Umm al-Darda', on the authority of Abu al-Darda', that he said: Nothing weighs heavier on the scale than good character. Ata' narrated it in the same way on the authority of Umm al-Darda'. Masruq narrated on the authority of Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, The best of you are those with the best character. Abdullah bin Abi Badr narrated to us, Muhammad bin Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Sarah, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: God rewards His servant for good character, just as He rewards the one who strives in the cause of God, going out and coming back with reward. Makhul narrated on the authority of Abu Tha'labah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The dearest of you to me and the closest to me in assembly are the best of you in character. The most hateful of you to me and the furthest from me in station in Paradise are the worst of you in character, the chatterers, the boasters, and the arrogant." Abu Uways narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Shall I not tell you about the most perfect of you in faith? The best of you in character, the most easy-going, the sociable and with whom others are sociable. Al-Layth narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Usamah on the authority of Bakr ibn Abi al-Furat who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: If God makes the creation and character of a man good, then the Fire will consume him. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ghalib al-Hadani on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Two characteristics will never come together in a believer: miserliness and bad character.” Maymun ibn Mihran said on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): There is no sin greater in the sight of God than bad character, because its perpetrator does not commit one sin except that he falls into another. He said: Ali ibn al-Ja’d narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us on the authority of a man from Quraysh who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is no sin greater in the sight of God than bad character. Good character melts away sins just as the sun melts ice, and bad character spoils deeds just as vinegar spoils honey.” Abdullah ibn Idris narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): You cannot satisfy people with your wealth, but you can satisfy them with a cheerful face and good character. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: Good character helps in religion. Chapter on the condemnation of arrogance Alqamah said on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that the Prophet said: He who has in his heart the weight of a grain of arrogance will not enter Paradise, and he who has in his heart the weight of a grain of faith will not enter Hell. Ibrahim bin Abi `Ubla said on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of `Abdullah bin `Amr, that the Prophet said: He who has in his heart the weight of an atom of arrogance, God will throw him on his face into Hell. Ishaq bin Isma`il told us, Abu Mu`awiyah told us on the authority of `Umar bin Rashid on the authority of Iyas bin Salamah on the authority of his father, that the Prophet said: A man will continue to go on his own until he is recorded with God as one of the tyrants, and then he will be afflicted with the punishment that afflicted them. Malik bin Dinar said: One day, Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them, rode the carpet with two hundred thousand humans and two hundred thousand jinn. It was raised until he heard the glorification of the angels in the sky. Then they lowered it until his feet touched the sea water. They heard a voice saying, If there had been an atom’s weight of arrogance in your master’s heart, it would have swallowed him up farther than he was raised. He said: Abu Khaithama told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: Abu Bakr used to give us a sermon and he would mention the beginning of the creation of man until one of us would defile himself and say, It came out of the urethra twice. Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever kills two people is a tyrant. Then he recited: Do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant on earth. Al-Hasan said: It is strange that the son of Adam washes his excrement with his hand twice a day, then he is arrogant, opposing the tyrant of the heavens. He said: Khalid bin Khidash told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Sufyan, then he mentioned a hadith in which the world is likened to what comes out of the son of Adam. Al-Hasan said, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of my father, who said: The food of the son of Adam is likened to the world, even if it is its rain and its salt. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Ali - from the descendants of Ali, may God be pleased with him - said: No amount of arrogance enters a man's heart except that his mind is diminished by that amount. Yunus ibn Ubayd said: There is no arrogance in prostration, nor is there hypocrisy in monotheism. Tawus looked at Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as he walked with arrogance, before he became caliph. Tawus poked him in the side with his finger and said: Isn’t this the way of someone who has feces in his stomach? He said to him as if apologizing to him: Uncle, every part of me was beaten for this walk until I learned it. Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: The Umayyads used to beat their children until they learned this walk. Chapter on swagger On the authority of Abu Layla, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever trails his garment out of arrogance, God will not look at him. And it was narrated on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ismail, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God will not look on the Day of Resurrection at whoever trails his garment. And while a man was swaggering in his two cloaks, admiring himself, God caused the earth to swallow him up, and he will continue sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection. And al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, While a man, and so on.
31:17: These are beneficial commandments that God the Almighty has narrated from Luqman the Wise, for people to comply with and follow. He said, O my son, indeed, if it be the weight of a mustard seed, meaning that even if the injustice or sin were the weight of a mustard seed, some of them allowed the pronoun in his saying it is to be a pronoun for the matter and the story, and on this basis it was allowed to raise weight, but the first is more appropriate. And the Almighty's saying, God will bring it forth, meaning God will bring it forth on the Day of Resurrection when He sets up the just scales, and will reward for it, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil, as God the Almighty said, And We will set up the Balance of Justice for the Day of Resurrection, so not a soul will be wronged at all, the verse. God Almighty said: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. Even if that atom were protected and veiled inside a solid rock, or absent and lost in the regions of the heavens and the earth, God would bring it to light, because nothing is hidden from Him, and not an atom’s weight in the heavens or the earth escapes Him. For this reason God Almighty said: Indeed, God is Kind and Aware. That is, He is Kind in knowledge, so nothing is hidden from Him, no matter how small, delicate, or insignificant they are. Aware of the crawling of an ant in the dark of night. Some of them claimed that what is meant by His statement, and it will be inside a rock, is a rock under the seven earths. Al-Suddi mentioned it with his chain of transmission, which is narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and a group of the Companions, if it is authentic. This is also narrated on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi, Abu Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Minhal bin Amr, and others. This - and God knows best - seems to have been received from the Israelite stories, which are neither truthful nor false. What appears - and God knows best - is that what is meant is that if this seed, despite its insignificance, were it to be inside a rock, God would reveal it and make it manifest with His subtle knowledge. As Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, If one of you were to work inside a solid rock that had no door or window, his work would be revealed to the people, whatever it may be. Then he said, O my son, establish prayer, meaning within its limits, obligations, and times. And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, meaning according to your ability and effort. And be patient over what befalls you. He knew that the one who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong will inevitably be harmed by the people, so He commanded him to be patient. His statement, Indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of resolve, means that patience in the face of people’s harm is for the one who has resolve. His statement, And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people, means do not turn your face away from people when you speak to them or they speak to you out of contempt for them and arrogance towards them. Rather, be gentle and smile at them, as it came in the hadith, Even if you meet your brother with your face beaming toward him, beware of letting your lower garment trail, for it is from conceit, and God does not like conceit. Ali ibn Abi Talha said that Ibn Abbas spoke about the verse, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning, do not be arrogant, thus belittling God's servants, and turn your face away from them when they speak to you. Al-Awfi and Ikrimah narrated this same verse from him. Malik said that Zaid ibn Aslam said, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning, do not speak while turning away. This was also narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Yazid ibn al-Asam, Abu al-Jawza', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and others. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said, He means speaking with a frown. The first statement is correct. Ibn Jarir said, "The root of sa'r is a disease that afflicts camels in their necks or heads, until their necks are torn away from their heads, so it is used to describe an arrogant man. This is the origin of the statement of Amr ibn Hayyi al-Taghlabi." And when the tyrant turned his cheek, we rose up to face him from his sway. Abu Talib said in his poetry: In the past, we did not accept injustice. If they bent their heads, we would correct them. His statement, And do not walk upon the earth exultantly, meaning arrogantly, haughtily, and stubbornly. Do not do that, and God will hate you. That is why He said, Indeed, God does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful, meaning one who is arrogant and conceited, proud of himself or others. And God the Almighty said, "And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height." We have already discussed this in its proper place. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami told us, Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Abi Laila told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who said: Arrogance was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he emphasized it, saying, God does not love any arrogant boaster. A man from among the people said, By God, O Messenger of God, when I wash my clothes, I like their whiteness, and I like the strap of my sandals and the strap of my whip. He said, “That is not arrogance. Arrogance is to belittle the truth and look down on people.” And he narrated it from another chain of transmission in a similar manner, and in it is a long story, and the killing of Thabit and his will after his death. His saying, And be moderate in your walk, means walk moderately, neither slow and hesitant, nor excessively fast, but rather walk in a moderate manner. His saying, And lower your voice, means do not exaggerate in your speech and do not raise your voice over anything that is useless. For this reason, he said, The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys. Mujahid and others said: The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys, meaning that the ultimate goal of raising one’s voice is that it resembles donkeys in its loudness and height, and despite this, it is hateful to God Almighty. This likening of donkeys in this case requires that it be forbidden and strongly condemned, because the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, “There is no evil example for us: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit.” Al-Nasa’i said in his interpretation of this verse: Qutaybah ibn Sa’id told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If you hear the crowing of roosters, then ask God for His bounty. And if you hear the braying of donkeys, then seek refuge in God from Satan, for they have seen Satan.” The rest of the group, except Ibn Majah, narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on his authority. In some versions: at night. And God knows best. These are very beneficial pieces of advice, and they are from the stories of Luqman the Wise from the Qur’an. Many wise sayings and sermons have been narrated from him, so let us mention a model and a constitution for that. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Sufyan told us, Nahshal ibn Majma’ al-Dhabi told me, on the authority of Qaz’ah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) told us, “Verily, Luqman the Wise used to say: ‘When God entrusts something to Him, He protects it.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Musa ibn Sulayman, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Luqman said to his son while admonishing him, ‘O my son, beware of covering your face, for it is frightening at night and reprehensible during the day.’ He said: My father told us, Amr bin Othman told us, on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Al-Tharri bin Yahya, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, wisdom has seated the poor in the company of kings. He also said: My father told us, Abdah bin Sulaiman told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Abdul Rahman Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, when you come to a gathering of people, shoot them with the arrow of Islam, meaning peace, then sit in their corner and do not speak until you see that they have spoken. If they are engrossed in the remembrance of God, then extend your arrow with them, but if they are engrossed in something else, then move on to someone else. He also said: My father told us, Amr bin Saeed bin Katheer bin Dinar told us, Damrah told us on the authority of Hafs bin Omar, who said: Luqman placed a bag of mustard next to him, and he began to admonish his son and take out a mustard seed until the mustard ran out. Then he said: O my son, I have admonished you with an admonition that if a mountain were admonished with it, it would crack. So his son cracked. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn Abd al-Baqi al-Masisi told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Harrani told us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Taraifi told us, Anas ibn Sufyan al-Maqdisi told us, on the authority of Khalifa ibn Salam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Take the blacks as your wives, for three of them are among the leaders of the people of Paradise: Luqman the Wise, the Negus, and Bilal the muezzin.” Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: He meant the Abyssinians. Chapter on idleness and humility This is related to the will of Luqman, peace be upon him, to his son. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya compiled a separate book on this, and we will mention its objectives from it. He said: Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir told us, Abdullah bin Musa Al-Madani told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid bin Hafs bin Abdullah bin Anas, on the authority of his grandfather Anas bin Malik, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, There may be a disheveled man wearing two cloaks who turns away from people’s doors, but when he swears an oath by God, God fulfills his oath. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Ja’far bin Sulayman, on the authority of Thabit, and Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it, and he added, Among them is Al-Bara’ bin Malik. Abu Bakr bin Sahl Al-Tamimi said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Nafi’ bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayyash bin Abbas, on the authority of Isa bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar may God be pleased with him, that he entered the mosque and saw Muadh bin Jabal weeping at the grave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said to him: What makes you weep, Muadh? He said: A hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I heard him say: “A little showing off is polytheism, and God loves the pious, the hidden, the wealthy, who, when absent, are not missed, and when present, are not recognized. Their hearts are lamps of guidance, and they are saved from every dark cloud.” Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ narrated to us, Affan ibn Ali narrated to us, on the authority of Humaid ibn Ata’ al-A’raj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said, “There may be a man of two cloaks who is not paid attention to, if he were to swear by God, He would fulfill his oath. If he were to say, ‘O God, I ask You for Paradise,’ He would give him Paradise and would not give him anything of this world.” He also said, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Among my nation is he who, if he came to the door of one of you and asked Him for a dinar or a dirham or a fils, He would not give it to him. If he asked God for Paradise, He would give it to him. If he asked Him for the world, He would not give it to him, nor would He withhold it from him because of its insignificance to him. He is a man of two cloaks who is not paid attention to, if he were to swear by God, He would fulfill his oath.” This is a mursal hadith from this chain of transmission. He also said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman told us, Awf told us, Abu Hurayrah said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Among the kings of Paradise are those who are disheveled and dusty, wearing two cloaks, and no one pays attention to them. They are those who, when they ask permission to see the rulers, are not given permission, and when they propose marriage to women, they are not married to them, and when they speak, they are not listened to. The needs of each one of them are churning in his chest. If his light were divided among the people on the Day of Resurrection, it would suffice them.” He said: Umar ibn Shabbah recited to me on the authority of Ibn Aishah, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Is there not a man with two cloaks in a house whose carpets are scattered and whose bedspreads are covered with rugs? His rivers flowed around his palace, and his gardens shone and surrounded him. It was also narrated from the hadith of Ubaidullah bin Zahr, from Ali bin Zaid, from Al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God said: ‘The most envied of My friends is a believer who is light-hearted, has a share of prayer, worships his Lord well and obeys Him in secret, and is obscure among the people and is not pointed at with fingers if he is patient in that.’” He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his hand in his pocket and said: His death hastened, his inheritance is small, and those who mourn him are few. And from Abdullah bin Amr, he said: The most beloved of God’s servants to God are the strangers. It was said: Who are the strangers? He said: Those who fled with their religion will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection to Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: I have been told that God the Almighty will say to the servant on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Did I not bestow blessings upon you, did I not give you, did I not cover you? Did I not... did I not... did I not humble your memory? Then Al-Fudayl said: If you can avoid being known, then do so. It does not matter if you are not praised, and it does not matter if you are blamed by people but praised by God. Ibn Muhayriz used to say: O God, I ask You for a humble memory. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad used to say: O God, make me among the highest of Your creation in Your sight, and make me among the lowest of Your creation in my own eyes, and among the people among Your average creation. Chapter on what was said about fame Then he said: Ahmad bin Isa Al-Masry told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Harith and Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Sinan bin Sa’d, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “It is enough for a man to be protected from evil, except for the one whom God has protected, that people point fingers at him in his religion and his worldly life. God does not look at your outward appearance, but at your hearts and your deeds.” And something similar was narrated on the authority of Ishaq bin Al-Bahlol, on the authority of Ibn Abi Fadik, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul-Wahid Al-Akhnasi, on the authority of Abdul-Wahid bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like this. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said to Al-Hasan: You are being pointed at with fingers, so he said: What is meant is the one who is pointed at in his religion with innovation and in his worldly life with immorality. On the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, he said: Do not start to become famous, and do not raise your person to be remembered, and learn but keep quiet, and be silent so that you will be safe, please the righteous and enrage the wicked. Ibrahim bin Adham may God have mercy on him said: He who loves fame has not spoken the truth about God. Ayoub said: No servant has spoken the truth about God except that he would be pleased not to know his place. Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ said: He who loves God loves that people do not know him. Samak bin Salamah said: Beware of having many friends. Abaan bin Othman said: If you want your religion to be safe, then have fewer acquaintances. If more than three people sat with Abu Al-Aaliyah, he would get up and leave them. He said: Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: Talha saw some people walking with him and said: They are flies of greed and moths of Hellfire. Ibn Idris narrated on the authority of Harun ibn Ibn Antara on the authority of Salim ibn Hanzala who said: While we were with my father, Umar ibn al-Khattab struck him with a whip and said: This is a humiliation for the follower and a trial for the followed. Ibn Awn narrated on the authority of al-Hasan: Ibn Masoud went out and some people followed him. He said: By God, if you knew why my door was locked, not two men among you would follow me. Hammad ibn Zayd said: When we passed by a gathering and Ayyub was with us and greeted us, they would respond vehemently, which would upset him. Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar: Ayyub used to make his shirt long, and he was asked about that. He said: Fame in the past was in the length of the shirt, but today it is in rolling it up. He once made sandals similar to those worn by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He wore them for a few days, then took them off and said: I have never seen people wearing them. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: Do not wear clothes that make scholars famous or that make fools look down on you. Al-Thawri said: They disliked fine clothing that would make one famous and in which people would raise their eyes to him, and poor clothing that would make one look despised and humiliate one’s religion. Khalid bin Khidash narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hasana, the companion of Al-Ziyadi, who said: We were with Abu Qilabah when a man wearing cloaks entered upon him. He said: Beware of this braying donkey. Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said: There are people who have placed arrogance in their hearts and humility in their clothing. The one wearing a cloak is greater with his cloak than the one wearing a cloak with his cloak. Why do they miss each other? In some reports, it is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, said to the Children of Israel: Why do you come to me wearing the clothing of monks, while your hearts are the hearts of wolves? Wear the clothing of kings, and soften your hearts with fear. Chapter on good character Abu At-Tayyah said on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was one of the best people in character. And on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Umar: It was said, O Messenger of God, which of the believers is best? He said, The one with the best character. And on the authority of Nuh ibn Abbad on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), “Indeed, a servant may attain, through his good character, the ranks of the Hereafter and the noblest of stations, even though he is weak in worship, and he may attain, through his bad character, the depths of Hellfire, even though he is a worshipper.” And on the authority of Sayyar ibn Harun on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Good character takes away the best of this world and the Hereafter. And on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Indeed, a servant may attain, through his good character, the rank of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts during the day. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Abu Muslim Abd Al-Rahman bin Yunus told me, Abdullah bin Idris told us, my father and uncle told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the thing that most often admits people to Paradise, and he said, Fear of God and good character. And he was asked about the thing that most often admits people to Hell, and he said, “The two hollows: the mouth and the private parts.” Usamah bin Sharik said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Bedouins came to him from every direction and said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?’ He said, ‘Good character.’” Ya'la bin Samak said, on the authority of Umm al-Darda', on the authority of Abu al-Darda', that he said: Nothing weighs heavier on the scale than good character. Ata' narrated it in the same way on the authority of Umm al-Darda'. Masruq narrated on the authority of Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, The best of you are those with the best character. Abdullah bin Abi Badr narrated to us, Muhammad bin Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Sarah, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: God rewards His servant for good character, just as He rewards the one who strives in the cause of God, going out and coming back with reward. Makhul narrated on the authority of Abu Tha'labah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The dearest of you to me and the closest to me in assembly are the best of you in character. The most hateful of you to me and the furthest from me in station in Paradise are the worst of you in character, the chatterers, the boasters, and the arrogant." Abu Uways narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Shall I not tell you about the most perfect of you in faith? The best of you in character, the most easy-going, the sociable and with whom others are sociable. Al-Layth narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Usamah on the authority of Bakr ibn Abi al-Furat who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: If God makes the creation and character of a man good, then the Fire will consume him. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ghalib al-Hadani on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Two characteristics will never come together in a believer: miserliness and bad character.” Maymun ibn Mihran said on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): There is no sin greater in the sight of God than bad character, because its perpetrator does not commit one sin except that he falls into another. He said: Ali ibn al-Ja’d narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us on the authority of a man from Quraysh who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is no sin greater in the sight of God than bad character. Good character melts away sins just as the sun melts ice, and bad character spoils deeds just as vinegar spoils honey.” Abdullah ibn Idris narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): You cannot satisfy people with your wealth, but you can satisfy them with a cheerful face and good character. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: Good character helps in religion. Chapter on the condemnation of arrogance Alqamah said on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that the Prophet said: He who has in his heart the weight of a grain of arrogance will not enter Paradise, and he who has in his heart the weight of a grain of faith will not enter Hell. Ibrahim bin Abi `Ubla said on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of `Abdullah bin `Amr, that the Prophet said: He who has in his heart the weight of an atom of arrogance, God will throw him on his face into Hell. Ishaq bin Isma`il told us, Abu Mu`awiyah told us on the authority of `Umar bin Rashid on the authority of Iyas bin Salamah on the authority of his father, that the Prophet said: A man will continue to go on his own until he is recorded with God as one of the tyrants, and then he will be afflicted with the punishment that afflicted them. Malik bin Dinar said: One day, Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them, rode the carpet with two hundred thousand humans and two hundred thousand jinn. It was raised until he heard the glorification of the angels in the sky. Then they lowered it until his feet touched the sea water. They heard a voice saying, If there had been an atom’s weight of arrogance in your master’s heart, it would have swallowed him up farther than he was raised. He said: Abu Khaithama told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: Abu Bakr used to give us a sermon and he would mention the beginning of the creation of man until one of us would defile himself and say, It came out of the urethra twice. Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever kills two people is a tyrant. Then he recited: Do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant on earth. Al-Hasan said: It is strange that the son of Adam washes his excrement with his hand twice a day, then he is arrogant, opposing the tyrant of the heavens. He said: Khalid bin Khidash told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Sufyan, then he mentioned a hadith in which the world is likened to what comes out of the son of Adam. Al-Hasan said, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of my father, who said: The food of the son of Adam is likened to the world, even if it is its rain and its salt. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Ali - from the descendants of Ali, may God be pleased with him - said: No amount of arrogance enters a man's heart except that his mind is diminished by that amount. Yunus ibn Ubayd said: There is no arrogance in prostration, nor is there hypocrisy in monotheism. Tawus looked at Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as he walked with arrogance, before he became caliph. Tawus poked him in the side with his finger and said: Isn’t this the way of someone who has feces in his stomach? He said to him as if apologizing to him: Uncle, every part of me was beaten for this walk until I learned it. Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: The Umayyads used to beat their children until they learned this walk. Chapter on swagger On the authority of Abu Layla, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever trails his garment out of arrogance, God will not look at him. And it was narrated on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ismail, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God will not look on the Day of Resurrection at whoever trails his garment. And while a man was swaggering in his two cloaks, admiring himself, God caused the earth to swallow him up, and he will continue sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection. And al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, While a man, and so on.
31:18: These are beneficial commandments that God the Almighty has narrated from Luqman the Wise, for people to comply with and follow. He said, O my son, indeed, if it be the weight of a mustard seed, meaning that even if the injustice or sin were the weight of a mustard seed, some of them allowed the pronoun in his saying it is to be a pronoun for the matter and the story, and on this basis it was allowed to raise weight, but the first is more appropriate. And the Almighty's saying, God will bring it forth, meaning God will bring it forth on the Day of Resurrection when He sets up the just scales, and will reward for it, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil, as God the Almighty said, And We will set up the Balance of Justice for the Day of Resurrection, so not a soul will be wronged at all, the verse. God Almighty said: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. Even if that atom were protected and veiled inside a solid rock, or absent and lost in the regions of the heavens and the earth, God would bring it to light, because nothing is hidden from Him, and not an atom’s weight in the heavens or the earth escapes Him.
