For this reason God Almighty said: Indeed, God is Kind and Aware. That is, He is Kind in knowledge, so nothing is hidden from Him, no matter how small, delicate, or insignificant they are. Aware of the crawling of an ant in the dark of night. Some of them claimed that what is meant by His statement, and it will be inside a rock, is a rock under the seven earths. Al-Suddi mentioned it with his chain of transmission, which is narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and a group of the Companions, if it is authentic. This is also narrated on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi, Abu Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Minhal bin Amr, and others. This - and God knows best - seems to have been received from the Israelite stories, which are neither truthful nor false. What appears - and God knows best - is that what is meant is that if this seed, despite its insignificance, were it to be inside a rock, God would reveal it and make it manifest with His subtle knowledge. As Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, If one of you were to work inside a solid rock that had no door or window, his work would be revealed to the people, whatever it may be. Then he said, O my son, establish prayer, meaning within its limits, obligations, and times. And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, meaning according to your ability and effort. And be patient over what befalls you. He knew that the one who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong will inevitably be harmed by the people, so He commanded him to be patient. His statement, Indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of resolve, means that patience in the face of people’s harm is for the one who has resolve. His statement, And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people, means do not turn your face away from people when you speak to them or they speak to you out of contempt for them and arrogance towards them. Rather, be gentle and smile at them, as it came in the hadith, Even if you meet your brother with your face beaming toward him, beware of letting your lower garment trail, for it is from conceit, and God does not like conceit. Ali ibn Abi Talha said that Ibn Abbas spoke about the verse, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning, do not be arrogant, thus belittling God's servants, and turn your face away from them when they speak to you. Al-Awfi and Ikrimah narrated this same verse from him. Malik said that Zaid ibn Aslam said, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning, do not speak while turning away. This was also narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Yazid ibn al-Asam, Abu al-Jawza', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and others. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said, He means speaking with a frown. The first statement is correct. Ibn Jarir said, "The root of sa'r is a disease that afflicts camels in their necks or heads, until their necks are torn away from their heads, so it is used to describe an arrogant man. This is the origin of the statement of Amr ibn Hayyi al-Taghlabi." And when the tyrant turned his cheek, we rose up to face him from his sway. Abu Talib said in his poetry: In the past, we did not accept injustice. If they bent their heads, we would correct them. His statement, And do not walk upon the earth exultantly, meaning arrogantly, haughtily, and stubbornly. Do not do that, and God will hate you. That is why He said, Indeed, God does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful, meaning one who is arrogant and conceited, proud of himself or others. And God the Almighty said, "And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height." We have already discussed this in its proper place. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami told us, Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Abi Laila told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who said: Arrogance was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he emphasized it, saying, God does not love any arrogant boaster. A man from among the people said, By God, O Messenger of God, when I wash my clothes, I like their whiteness, and I like the strap of my sandals and the strap of my whip. He said, “That is not arrogance. Arrogance is to belittle the truth and look down on people.” And he narrated it from another chain of transmission in a similar manner, and in it is a long story, and the killing of Thabit and his will after his death. His saying, And be moderate in your walk, means walk moderately, neither slow and hesitant, nor excessively fast, but rather walk in a moderate manner. His saying, And lower your voice, means do not exaggerate in your speech and do not raise your voice over anything that is useless. For this reason, he said, The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys. Mujahid and others said: The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys, meaning that the ultimate goal of raising one’s voice is that it resembles donkeys in its loudness and height, and despite this, it is hateful to God Almighty. This likening of donkeys in this case requires that it be forbidden and strongly condemned, because the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, “There is no evil example for us: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit.” Al-Nasa’i said in his interpretation of this verse: Qutaybah ibn Sa’id told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If you hear the crowing of roosters, then ask God for His bounty. And if you hear the braying of donkeys, then seek refuge in God from Satan, for they have seen Satan.” The rest of the group, except Ibn Majah, narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on his authority. In some versions: at night. And God knows best. These are very beneficial pieces of advice, and they are from the stories of Luqman the Wise from the Qur’an. Many wise sayings and sermons have been narrated from him, so let us mention a model and a constitution for that. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Sufyan told us, Nahshal ibn Majma’ al-Dhabi told me, on the authority of Qaz’ah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) told us, “Verily, Luqman the Wise used to say: ‘When God entrusts something to Him, He protects it.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Musa ibn Sulayman, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Luqman said to his son while admonishing him, ‘O my son, beware of covering your face, for it is frightening at night and reprehensible during the day.’ He said: My father told us, Amr bin Othman told us, on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Al-Tharri bin Yahya, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, wisdom has seated the poor in the company of kings. He also said: My father told us, Abdah bin Sulaiman told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Abdul Rahman Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, when you come to a gathering of people, shoot them with the arrow of Islam, meaning peace, then sit in their corner and do not speak until you see that they have spoken. If they are engrossed in the remembrance of God, then extend your arrow with them, but if they are engrossed in something else, then move on to someone else. He also said: My father told us, Amr bin Saeed bin Katheer bin Dinar told us, Damrah told us on the authority of Hafs bin Omar, who said: Luqman placed a bag of mustard next to him, and he began to admonish his son and take out a mustard seed until the mustard ran out. Then he said: O my son, I have admonished you with an admonition that if a mountain were admonished with it, it would crack. So his son cracked. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn Abd al-Baqi al-Masisi told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Harrani told us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Taraifi told us, Anas ibn Sufyan al-Maqdisi told us, on the authority of Khalifa ibn Salam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Take the blacks as your wives, for three of them are among the leaders of the people of Paradise: Luqman the Wise, the Negus, and Bilal the muezzin.” Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: He meant the Abyssinians. Chapter on idleness and humility This is related to the will of Luqman, peace be upon him, to his son. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya compiled a separate book on this, and we will mention its objectives from it. He said: Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir told us, Abdullah bin Musa Al-Madani told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid bin Hafs bin Abdullah bin Anas, on the authority of his grandfather Anas bin Malik, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, There may be a disheveled man wearing two cloaks who turns away from people’s doors, but when he swears an oath by God, God fulfills his oath. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Ja’far bin Sulayman, on the authority of Thabit, and Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it, and he added, Among them is Al-Bara’ bin Malik. Abu Bakr bin Sahl Al-Tamimi said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Nafi’ bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayyash bin Abbas, on the authority of Isa bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar may God be pleased with him, that he entered the mosque and saw Muadh bin Jabal weeping at the grave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said to him: What makes you weep, Muadh? He said: A hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I heard him say: “A little showing off is polytheism, and God loves the pious, the hidden, the wealthy, who, when absent, are not missed, and when present, are not recognized. Their hearts are lamps of guidance, and they are saved from every dark cloud.” Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ narrated to us, Affan ibn Ali narrated to us, on the authority of Humaid ibn Ata’ al-A’raj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said, “There may be a man of two cloaks who is not paid attention to, if he were to swear by God, He would fulfill his oath. If he were to say, ‘O God, I ask You for Paradise,’ He would give him Paradise and would not give him anything of this world.” He also said, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Among my nation is he who, if he came to the door of one of you and asked Him for a dinar or a dirham or a fils, He would not give it to him. If he asked God for Paradise, He would give it to him. If he asked Him for the world, He would not give it to him, nor would He withhold it from him because of its insignificance to him. He is a man of two cloaks who is not paid attention to, if he were to swear by God, He would fulfill his oath.” This is a mursal hadith from this chain of transmission. He also said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman told us, Awf told us, Abu Hurayrah said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Among the kings of Paradise are those who are disheveled and dusty, wearing two cloaks, and no one pays attention to them. They are those who, when they ask permission to see the rulers, are not given permission, and when they propose marriage to women, they are not married to them, and when they speak, they are not listened to. The needs of each one of them are churning in his chest. If his light were divided among the people on the Day of Resurrection, it would suffice them.” He said: Umar ibn Shabbah recited to me on the authority of Ibn Aishah, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Is there not a man with two cloaks in a house whose carpets are scattered and whose bedspreads are covered with rugs? His rivers flowed around his palace, and his gardens shone and surrounded him. It was also narrated from the hadith of Ubaidullah bin Zahr, from Ali bin Zaid, from Al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God said: ‘The most envied of My friends is a believer who is light-hearted, has a share of prayer, worships his Lord well and obeys Him in secret, and is obscure among the people and is not pointed at with fingers if he is patient in that.’” He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his hand in his pocket and said: His death hastened, his inheritance is small, and those who mourn him are few. And from Abdullah bin Amr, he said: The most beloved of God’s servants to God are the strangers. It was said: Who are the strangers? He said: Those who fled with their religion will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection to Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: I have been told that God the Almighty will say to the servant on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Did I not bestow blessings upon you, did I not give you, did I not cover you? Did I not... did I not... did I not humble your memory? Then Al-Fudayl said: If you can avoid being known, then do so. It does not matter if you are not praised, and it does not matter if you are blamed by people but praised by God. Ibn Muhayriz used to say: O God, I ask You for a humble memory. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad used to say: O God, make me among the highest of Your creation in Your sight, and make me among the lowest of Your creation in my own eyes, and among the people among Your average creation. Chapter on what was said about fame Then he said: Ahmad bin Isa Al-Masry told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Harith and Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Sinan bin Sa’d, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “It is enough for a man to be protected from evil, except for the one whom God has protected, that people point fingers at him in his religion and his worldly life. God does not look at your outward appearance, but at your hearts and your deeds.” And something similar was narrated on the authority of Ishaq bin Al-Bahlol, on the authority of Ibn Abi Fadik, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul-Wahid Al-Akhnasi, on the authority of Abdul-Wahid bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like this. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said to Al-Hasan: You are being pointed at with fingers, so he said: What is meant is the one who is pointed at in his religion with innovation and in his worldly life with immorality. On the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, he said: Do not start to become famous, and do not raise your person to be remembered, and learn but keep quiet, and be silent so that you will be safe, please the righteous and enrage the wicked. Ibrahim bin Adham may God have mercy on him said: He who loves fame has not spoken the truth about God. Ayoub said: No servant has spoken the truth about God except that he would be pleased not to know his place. Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ said: He who loves God loves that people do not know him. Samak bin Salamah said: Beware of having many friends. Abaan bin Othman said: If you want your religion to be safe, then have fewer acquaintances. If more than three people sat with Abu Al-Aaliyah, he would get up and leave them. He said: Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: Talha saw some people walking with him and said: They are flies of greed and moths of Hellfire. Ibn Idris narrated on the authority of Harun ibn Ibn Antara on the authority of Salim ibn Hanzala who said: While we were with my father, Umar ibn al-Khattab struck him with a whip and said: This is a humiliation for the follower and a trial for the followed. Ibn Awn narrated on the authority of al-Hasan: Ibn Masoud went out and some people followed him. He said: By God, if you knew why my door was locked, not two men among you would follow me. Hammad ibn Zayd said: When we passed by a gathering and Ayyub was with us and greeted us, they would respond vehemently, which would upset him. Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar: Ayyub used to make his shirt long, and he was asked about that. He said: Fame in the past was in the length of the shirt, but today it is in rolling it up. He once made sandals similar to those worn by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He wore them for a few days, then took them off and said: I have never seen people wearing them. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: Do not wear clothes that make scholars famous or that make fools look down on you. Al-Thawri said: They disliked fine clothing that would make one famous and in which people would raise their eyes to him, and poor clothing that would make one look despised and humiliate one’s religion. Khalid bin Khidash narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hasana, the companion of Al-Ziyadi, who said: We were with Abu Qilabah when a man wearing cloaks entered upon him. He said: Beware of this braying donkey. Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said: There are people who have placed arrogance in their hearts and humility in their clothing. The one wearing a cloak is greater with his cloak than the one wearing a cloak with his cloak. Why do they miss each other? In some reports, it is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, said to the Children of Israel: Why do you come to me wearing the clothing of monks, while your hearts are the hearts of wolves? Wear the clothing of kings, and soften your hearts with fear. Chapter on good character Abu At-Tayyah said on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was one of the best people in character. And on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Umar: It was said, O Messenger of God, which of the believers is best? He said, The one with the best character. And on the authority of Nuh ibn Abbad on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), “Indeed, a servant may attain, through his good character, the ranks of the Hereafter and the noblest of stations, even though he is weak in worship, and he may attain, through his bad character, the depths of Hellfire, even though he is a worshipper.” And on the authority of Sayyar ibn Harun on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Good character takes away the best of this world and the Hereafter. And on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Indeed, a servant may attain, through his good character, the rank of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts during the day. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Abu Muslim Abd Al-Rahman bin Yunus told me, Abdullah bin Idris told us, my father and uncle told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the thing that most often admits people to Paradise, and he said, Fear of God and good character. And he was asked about the thing that most often admits people to Hell, and he said, “The two hollows: the mouth and the private parts.” Usamah bin Sharik said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Bedouins came to him from every direction and said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?’ He said, ‘Good character.’” Ya'la bin Samak said, on the authority of Umm al-Darda', on the authority of Abu al-Darda', that he said: Nothing weighs heavier on the scale than good character. Ata' narrated it in the same way on the authority of Umm al-Darda'. Masruq narrated on the authority of Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, The best of you are those with the best character. Abdullah bin Abi Badr narrated to us, Muhammad bin Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Sarah, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: God rewards His servant for good character, just as He rewards the one who strives in the cause of God, going out and coming back with reward. Makhul narrated on the authority of Abu Tha'labah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The dearest of you to me and the closest to me in assembly are the best of you in character. The most hateful of you to me and the furthest from me in station in Paradise are the worst of you in character, the chatterers, the boasters, and the arrogant." Abu Uways narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Shall I not tell you about the most perfect of you in faith? The best of you in character, the most easy-going, the sociable and with whom others are sociable. Al-Layth narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Usamah on the authority of Bakr ibn Abi al-Furat who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: If God makes the creation and character of a man good, then the Fire will consume him. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ghalib al-Hadani on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Two characteristics will never come together in a believer: miserliness and bad character.” Maymun ibn Mihran said on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): There is no sin greater in the sight of God than bad character, because its perpetrator does not commit one sin except that he falls into another. He said: Ali ibn al-Ja’d narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us on the authority of a man from Quraysh who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is no sin greater in the sight of God than bad character. Good character melts away sins just as the sun melts ice, and bad character spoils deeds just as vinegar spoils honey.” Abdullah ibn Idris narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): You cannot satisfy people with your wealth, but you can satisfy them with a cheerful face and good character. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: Good character helps in religion. Chapter on the condemnation of arrogance Alqamah said on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that the Prophet said: He who has in his heart the weight of a grain of arrogance will not enter Paradise, and he who has in his heart the weight of a grain of faith will not enter Hell. Ibrahim bin Abi `Ubla said on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of `Abdullah bin `Amr, that the Prophet said: He who has in his heart the weight of an atom of arrogance, God will throw him on his face into Hell. Ishaq bin Isma`il told us, Abu Mu`awiyah told us on the authority of `Umar bin Rashid on the authority of Iyas bin Salamah on the authority of his father, that the Prophet said: A man will continue to go on his own until he is recorded with God as one of the tyrants, and then he will be afflicted with the punishment that afflicted them. Malik bin Dinar said: One day, Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them, rode the carpet with two hundred thousand humans and two hundred thousand jinn. It was raised until he heard the glorification of the angels in the sky. Then they lowered it until his feet touched the sea water. They heard a voice saying, If there had been an atom’s weight of arrogance in your master’s heart, it would have swallowed him up farther than he was raised. He said: Abu Khaithama told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: Abu Bakr used to give us a sermon and he would mention the beginning of the creation of man until one of us would defile himself and say, It came out of the urethra twice. Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever kills two people is a tyrant. Then he recited: Do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant on earth. Al-Hasan said: It is strange that the son of Adam washes his excrement with his hand twice a day, then he is arrogant, opposing the tyrant of the heavens. He said: Khalid bin Khidash told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Sufyan, then he mentioned a hadith in which the world is likened to what comes out of the son of Adam. Al-Hasan said, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of my father, who said: The food of the son of Adam is likened to the world, even if it is its rain and its salt. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Ali - from the descendants of Ali, may God be pleased with him - said: No amount of arrogance enters a man's heart except that his mind is diminished by that amount. Yunus ibn Ubayd said: There is no arrogance in prostration, nor is there hypocrisy in monotheism. Tawus looked at Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as he walked with arrogance, before he became caliph. Tawus poked him in the side with his finger and said: Isn’t this the way of someone who has feces in his stomach? He said to him as if apologizing to him: Uncle, every part of me was beaten for this walk until I learned it. Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: The Umayyads used to beat their children until they learned this walk. Chapter on swagger On the authority of Abu Layla, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever trails his garment out of arrogance, God will not look at him. And it was narrated on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ismail, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God will not look on the Day of Resurrection at whoever trails his garment. And while a man was swaggering in his two cloaks, admiring himself, God caused the earth to swallow him up, and he will continue sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection. And al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, While a man, and so on.
31:19: These are beneficial commandments that God the Almighty has narrated from Luqman the Wise, for people to comply with and follow. He said, O my son, indeed, if it be the weight of a mustard seed, meaning that even if the injustice or sin were the weight of a mustard seed, some of them allowed the pronoun in his saying it is to be a pronoun for the matter and the story, and on this basis it was allowed to raise weight, but the first is more appropriate. And the Almighty's saying, God will bring it forth, meaning God will bring it forth on the Day of Resurrection when He sets up the just scales, and will reward for it, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil, as God the Almighty said, And We will set up the Balance of Justice for the Day of Resurrection, so not a soul will be wronged at all, the verse. God Almighty said: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. Even if that atom were protected and veiled inside a solid rock, or absent and lost in the regions of the heavens and the earth, God would bring it to light, because nothing is hidden from Him, and not an atom’s weight in the heavens or the earth escapes Him. For this reason God Almighty said: Indeed, God is Kind and Aware. That is, He is Kind in knowledge, so nothing is hidden from Him, no matter how small, delicate, or insignificant they are. Aware of the crawling of an ant in the dark of night. Some of them claimed that what is meant by His statement, and it will be inside a rock, is a rock under the seven earths. Al-Suddi mentioned it with his chain of transmission, which is narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and a group of the Companions, if it is authentic. This is also narrated on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Awfi, Abu Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Minhal bin Amr, and others. This - and God knows best - seems to have been received from the Israelite stories, which are neither truthful nor false. What appears - and God knows best - is that what is meant is that if this seed, despite its insignificance, were it to be inside a rock, God would reveal it and make it manifest with His subtle knowledge. As Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, If one of you were to work inside a solid rock that had no door or window, his work would be revealed to the people, whatever it may be. Then he said, O my son, establish prayer, meaning within its limits, obligations, and times. And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, meaning according to your ability and effort. And be patient over what befalls you. He knew that the one who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong will inevitably be harmed by the people, so He commanded him to be patient. His statement, Indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of resolve, means that patience in the face of people’s harm is for the one who has resolve. His statement, And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people, means do not turn your face away from people when you speak to them or they speak to you out of contempt for them and arrogance towards them. Rather, be gentle and smile at them, as it came in the hadith, Even if you meet your brother with your face beaming toward him, beware of letting your lower garment trail, for it is from conceit, and God does not like conceit. Ali ibn Abi Talha said that Ibn Abbas spoke about the verse, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning, do not be arrogant, thus belittling God's servants, and turn your face away from them when they speak to you. Al-Awfi and Ikrimah narrated this same verse from him. Malik said that Zaid ibn Aslam said, And do not turn your cheek away from people, meaning, do not speak while turning away. This was also narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Yazid ibn al-Asam, Abu al-Jawza', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and others. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said, He means speaking with a frown. The first statement is correct. Ibn Jarir said, "The root of sa'r is a disease that afflicts camels in their necks or heads, until their necks are torn away from their heads, so it is used to describe an arrogant man. This is the origin of the statement of Amr ibn Hayyi al-Taghlabi." And when the tyrant turned his cheek, we rose up to face him from his sway. Abu Talib said in his poetry: In the past, we did not accept injustice. If they bent their heads, we would correct them. His statement, And do not walk upon the earth exultantly, meaning arrogantly, haughtily, and stubbornly. Do not do that, and God will hate you. That is why He said, Indeed, God does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful, meaning one who is arrogant and conceited, proud of himself or others. And God the Almighty said, "And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height." We have already discussed this in its proper place. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami told us, Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Abi Laila told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who said: Arrogance was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he emphasized it, saying, God does not love any arrogant boaster. A man from among the people said, By God, O Messenger of God, when I wash my clothes, I like their whiteness, and I like the strap of my sandals and the strap of my whip. He said, “That is not arrogance. Arrogance is to belittle the truth and look down on people.” And he narrated it from another chain of transmission in a similar manner, and in it is a long story, and the killing of Thabit and his will after his death. His saying, And be moderate in your walk, means walk moderately, neither slow and hesitant, nor excessively fast, but rather walk in a moderate manner. His saying, And lower your voice, means do not exaggerate in your speech and do not raise your voice over anything that is useless. For this reason, he said, The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys. Mujahid and others said: The most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys, meaning that the ultimate goal of raising one’s voice is that it resembles donkeys in its loudness and height, and despite this, it is hateful to God Almighty. This likening of donkeys in this case requires that it be forbidden and strongly condemned, because the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, “There is no evil example for us: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit.” Al-Nasa’i said in his interpretation of this verse: Qutaybah ibn Sa’id told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If you hear the crowing of roosters, then ask God for His bounty. And if you hear the braying of donkeys, then seek refuge in God from Satan, for they have seen Satan.” The rest of the group, except Ibn Majah, narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah, on his authority. In some versions: at night. And God knows best. These are very beneficial pieces of advice, and they are from the stories of Luqman the Wise from the Qur’an. Many wise sayings and sermons have been narrated from him, so let us mention a model and a constitution for that. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Sufyan told us, Nahshal ibn Majma’ al-Dhabi told me, on the authority of Qaz’ah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) told us, “Verily, Luqman the Wise used to say: ‘When God entrusts something to Him, He protects it.’” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Musa ibn Sulayman, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Luqman said to his son while admonishing him, ‘O my son, beware of covering your face, for it is frightening at night and reprehensible during the day.’ He said: My father told us, Amr bin Othman told us, on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Al-Tharri bin Yahya, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, wisdom has seated the poor in the company of kings. He also said: My father told us, Abdah bin Sulaiman told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Abdul Rahman Al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, when you come to a gathering of people, shoot them with the arrow of Islam, meaning peace, then sit in their corner and do not speak until you see that they have spoken. If they are engrossed in the remembrance of God, then extend your arrow with them, but if they are engrossed in something else, then move on to someone else. He also said: My father told us, Amr bin Saeed bin Katheer bin Dinar told us, Damrah told us on the authority of Hafs bin Omar, who said: Luqman placed a bag of mustard next to him, and he began to admonish his son and take out a mustard seed until the mustard ran out. Then he said: O my son, I have admonished you with an admonition that if a mountain were admonished with it, it would crack. So his son cracked. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn Abd al-Baqi al-Masisi told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Harrani told us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Taraifi told us, Anas ibn Sufyan al-Maqdisi told us, on the authority of Khalifa ibn Salam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Take the blacks as your wives, for three of them are among the leaders of the people of Paradise: Luqman the Wise, the Negus, and Bilal the muezzin.” Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: He meant the Abyssinians. Chapter on idleness and humility This is related to the will of Luqman, peace be upon him, to his son. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Dunya compiled a separate book on this, and we will mention its objectives from it. He said: Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir told us, Abdullah bin Musa Al-Madani told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid bin Hafs bin Abdullah bin Anas, on the authority of his grandfather Anas bin Malik, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, There may be a disheveled man wearing two cloaks who turns away from people’s doors, but when he swears an oath by God, God fulfills his oath. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Ja’far bin Sulayman, on the authority of Thabit, and Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it, and he added, Among them is Al-Bara’ bin Malik. Abu Bakr bin Sahl Al-Tamimi said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Nafi’ bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayyash bin Abbas, on the authority of Isa bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar may God be pleased with him, that he entered the mosque and saw Muadh bin Jabal weeping at the grave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said to him: What makes you weep, Muadh? He said: A hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I heard him say: “A little showing off is polytheism, and God loves the pious, the hidden, the wealthy, who, when absent, are not missed, and when present, are not recognized. Their hearts are lamps of guidance, and they are saved from every dark cloud.” Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ narrated to us, Affan ibn Ali narrated to us, on the authority of Humaid ibn Ata’ al-A’raj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said, “There may be a man of two cloaks who is not paid attention to, if he were to swear by God, He would fulfill his oath. If he were to say, ‘O God, I ask You for Paradise,’ He would give him Paradise and would not give him anything of this world.” He also said, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Among my nation is he who, if he came to the door of one of you and asked Him for a dinar or a dirham or a fils, He would not give it to him. If he asked God for Paradise, He would give it to him. If he asked Him for the world, He would not give it to him, nor would He withhold it from him because of its insignificance to him. He is a man of two cloaks who is not paid attention to, if he were to swear by God, He would fulfill his oath.” This is a mursal hadith from this chain of transmission. He also said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman told us, Awf told us, Abu Hurayrah said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Among the kings of Paradise are those who are disheveled and dusty, wearing two cloaks, and no one pays attention to them. They are those who, when they ask permission to see the rulers, are not given permission, and when they propose marriage to women, they are not married to them, and when they speak, they are not listened to. The needs of each one of them are churning in his chest. If his light were divided among the people on the Day of Resurrection, it would suffice them.” He said: Umar ibn Shabbah recited to me on the authority of Ibn Aishah, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Is there not a man with two cloaks in a house whose carpets are scattered and whose bedspreads are covered with rugs? His rivers flowed around his palace, and his gardens shone and surrounded him. It was also narrated from the hadith of Ubaidullah bin Zahr, from Ali bin Zaid, from Al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God said: ‘The most envied of My friends is a believer who is light-hearted, has a share of prayer, worships his Lord well and obeys Him in secret, and is obscure among the people and is not pointed at with fingers if he is patient in that.’” He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his hand in his pocket and said: His death hastened, his inheritance is small, and those who mourn him are few. And from Abdullah bin Amr, he said: The most beloved of God’s servants to God are the strangers. It was said: Who are the strangers? He said: Those who fled with their religion will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection to Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: I have been told that God the Almighty will say to the servant on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Did I not bestow blessings upon you, did I not give you, did I not cover you? Did I not... did I not... did I not humble your memory? Then Al-Fudayl said: If you can avoid being known, then do so. It does not matter if you are not praised, and it does not matter if you are blamed by people but praised by God. Ibn Muhayriz used to say: O God, I ask You for a humble memory. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad used to say: O God, make me among the highest of Your creation in Your sight, and make me among the lowest of Your creation in my own eyes, and among the people among Your average creation. Chapter on what was said about fame Then he said: Ahmad bin Isa Al-Masry told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Harith and Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Sinan bin Sa’d, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “It is enough for a man to be protected from evil, except for the one whom God has protected, that people point fingers at him in his religion and his worldly life. God does not look at your outward appearance, but at your hearts and your deeds.” And something similar was narrated on the authority of Ishaq bin Al-Bahlol, on the authority of Ibn Abi Fadik, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul-Wahid Al-Akhnasi, on the authority of Abdul-Wahid bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like this. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said to Al-Hasan: You are being pointed at with fingers, so he said: What is meant is the one who is pointed at in his religion with innovation and in his worldly life with immorality. On the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, he said: Do not start to become famous, and do not raise your person to be remembered, and learn but keep quiet, and be silent so that you will be safe, please the righteous and enrage the wicked. Ibrahim bin Adham may God have mercy on him said: He who loves fame has not spoken the truth about God. Ayoub said: No servant has spoken the truth about God except that he would be pleased not to know his place. Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ said: He who loves God loves that people do not know him. Samak bin Salamah said: Beware of having many friends. Abaan bin Othman said: If you want your religion to be safe, then have fewer acquaintances. If more than three people sat with Abu Al-Aaliyah, he would get up and leave them. He said: Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: Talha saw some people walking with him and said: They are flies of greed and moths of Hellfire. Ibn Idris narrated on the authority of Harun ibn Ibn Antara on the authority of Salim ibn Hanzala who said: While we were with my father, Umar ibn al-Khattab struck him with a whip and said: This is a humiliation for the follower and a trial for the followed. Ibn Awn narrated on the authority of al-Hasan: Ibn Masoud went out and some people followed him. He said: By God, if you knew why my door was locked, not two men among you would follow me. Hammad ibn Zayd said: When we passed by a gathering and Ayyub was with us and greeted us, they would respond vehemently, which would upset him. Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar: Ayyub used to make his shirt long, and he was asked about that. He said: Fame in the past was in the length of the shirt, but today it is in rolling it up. He once made sandals similar to those worn by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He wore them for a few days, then took them off and said: I have never seen people wearing them. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: Do not wear clothes that make scholars famous or that make fools look down on you. Al-Thawri said: They disliked fine clothing that would make one famous and in which people would raise their eyes to him, and poor clothing that would make one look despised and humiliate one’s religion. Khalid bin Khidash narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hasana, the companion of Al-Ziyadi, who said: We were with Abu Qilabah when a man wearing cloaks entered upon him. He said: Beware of this braying donkey. Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said: There are people who have placed arrogance in their hearts and humility in their clothing. The one wearing a cloak is greater with his cloak than the one wearing a cloak with his cloak. Why do they miss each other? In some reports, it is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, said to the Children of Israel: Why do you come to me wearing the clothing of monks, while your hearts are the hearts of wolves? Wear the clothing of kings, and soften your hearts with fear. Chapter on good character Abu At-Tayyah said on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was one of the best people in character. And on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Umar: It was said, O Messenger of God, which of the believers is best? He said, The one with the best character. And on the authority of Nuh ibn Abbad on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), “Indeed, a servant may attain, through his good character, the ranks of the Hereafter and the noblest of stations, even though he is weak in worship, and he may attain, through his bad character, the depths of Hellfire, even though he is a worshipper.” And on the authority of Sayyar ibn Harun on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Good character takes away the best of this world and the Hereafter. And on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Indeed, a servant may attain, through his good character, the rank of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts during the day. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Abu Muslim Abd Al-Rahman bin Yunus told me, Abdullah bin Idris told us, my father and uncle told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the thing that most often admits people to Paradise, and he said, Fear of God and good character. And he was asked about the thing that most often admits people to Hell, and he said, “The two hollows: the mouth and the private parts.” Usamah bin Sharik said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Bedouins came to him from every direction and said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is the best thing given to a person?’ He said, ‘Good character.’” Ya'la bin Samak said, on the authority of Umm al-Darda', on the authority of Abu al-Darda', that he said: Nothing weighs heavier on the scale than good character. Ata' narrated it in the same way on the authority of Umm al-Darda'. Masruq narrated on the authority of Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, The best of you are those with the best character. Abdullah bin Abi Badr narrated to us, Muhammad bin Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Sarah, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: God rewards His servant for good character, just as He rewards the one who strives in the cause of God, going out and coming back with reward. Makhul narrated on the authority of Abu Tha'labah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The dearest of you to me and the closest to me in assembly are the best of you in character. The most hateful of you to me and the furthest from me in station in Paradise are the worst of you in character, the chatterers, the boasters, and the arrogant." Abu Uways narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Shall I not tell you about the most perfect of you in faith? The best of you in character, the most easy-going, the sociable and with whom others are sociable. Al-Layth narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Usamah on the authority of Bakr ibn Abi al-Furat who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: If God makes the creation and character of a man good, then the Fire will consume him. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ghalib al-Hadani on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Two characteristics will never come together in a believer: miserliness and bad character.” Maymun ibn Mihran said on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): There is no sin greater in the sight of God than bad character, because its perpetrator does not commit one sin except that he falls into another. He said: Ali ibn al-Ja’d narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us on the authority of a man from Quraysh who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is no sin greater in the sight of God than bad character. Good character melts away sins just as the sun melts ice, and bad character spoils deeds just as vinegar spoils honey.” Abdullah ibn Idris narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): You cannot satisfy people with your wealth, but you can satisfy them with a cheerful face and good character. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: Good character helps in religion. Chapter on the condemnation of arrogance Alqamah said on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that the Prophet said: He who has in his heart the weight of a grain of arrogance will not enter Paradise, and he who has in his heart the weight of a grain of faith will not enter Hell. Ibrahim bin Abi `Ubla said on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of `Abdullah bin `Amr, that the Prophet said: He who has in his heart the weight of an atom of arrogance, God will throw him on his face into Hell. Ishaq bin Isma`il told us, Abu Mu`awiyah told us on the authority of `Umar bin Rashid on the authority of Iyas bin Salamah on the authority of his father, that the Prophet said: A man will continue to go on his own until he is recorded with God as one of the tyrants, and then he will be afflicted with the punishment that afflicted them. Malik bin Dinar said: One day, Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them, rode the carpet with two hundred thousand humans and two hundred thousand jinn. It was raised until he heard the glorification of the angels in the sky. Then they lowered it until his feet touched the sea water. They heard a voice saying, If there had been an atom’s weight of arrogance in your master’s heart, it would have swallowed him up farther than he was raised. He said: Abu Khaithama told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: Abu Bakr used to give us a sermon and he would mention the beginning of the creation of man until one of us would defile himself and say, It came out of the urethra twice. Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever kills two people is a tyrant. Then he recited: Do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant on earth. Al-Hasan said: It is strange that the son of Adam washes his excrement with his hand twice a day, then he is arrogant, opposing the tyrant of the heavens. He said: Khalid bin Khidash told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Sufyan, then he mentioned a hadith in which the world is likened to what comes out of the son of Adam. Al-Hasan said, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of my father, who said: The food of the son of Adam is likened to the world, even if it is its rain and its salt. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Ali - from the descendants of Ali, may God be pleased with him - said: No amount of arrogance enters a man's heart except that his mind is diminished by that amount. Yunus ibn Ubayd said: There is no arrogance in prostration, nor is there hypocrisy in monotheism. Tawus looked at Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz as he walked with arrogance, before he became caliph. Tawus poked him in the side with his finger and said: Isn’t this the way of someone who has feces in his stomach? He said to him as if apologizing to him: Uncle, every part of me was beaten for this walk until I learned it. Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: The Umayyads used to beat their children until they learned this walk. Chapter on swagger On the authority of Abu Layla, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever trails his garment out of arrogance, God will not look at him. And it was narrated on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ismail, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God will not look on the Day of Resurrection at whoever trails his garment. And while a man was swaggering in his two cloaks, admiring himself, God caused the earth to swallow him up, and he will continue sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection. And al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, While a man, and so on.
31:20: God Almighty says, reminding His creation of His blessings upon them in this world and the Hereafter, that He has subjected to them what is in the heavens of stars by which they may be illuminated during their night and day, and what He creates in them of clouds, rain, snow, and hail, and He made them a protected roof for them, and what He created for them on the earth of settlements, rivers, trees, crops, and fruits, and He has bestowed upon them His apparent and hidden blessings of sending messengers, revealing books, and removing doubts and defects. Then, despite all of this, not all people believe. Rather, some of them dispute about God, that is, about His Oneness and sending messengers, and dispute with Him about that without knowledge, or support from a sound argument, or a sound transmitted book. For this reason, God Almighty said: And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book, that is, a clear, illuminating one. And when it is said to them, that is, to these disputants about the Oneness of God, Follow what God has revealed, that is, to His Messenger of the purified laws, they say, ‘Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing,’ that is, they did not… They have no argument except following their forefathers. God Almighty said: Or even if their fathers did not understand anything nor were they guided? That is, what do you think, you who argue with the actions of their forefathers, that they were in error and you are their successors in what they were in? For this reason God Almighty said: Or even if Satan were inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze.

31:22: God Almighty says, informing about the one who submits his face to God, that is, sincerely works for Him, submits to His command, and follows His law. For this reason, He said, and he is a doer of good, that is, in his work by following what He has commanded and leaving what He has forbidden. He has grasped the most trustworthy handhold, that is, he has taken a firm pledge from God that will not be punished. “And to God is the outcome of all matters. And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you,” that is, do not grieve over them, O Muhammad, in their disbelief in God and what you have brought, for God’s decree is effective against them, and to God is their return, and He will inform them of what they have done, that is, He will reward them for it. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts, so nothing is hidden from Him. Then God Almighty said, We grant them enjoyment for a little, that is, in this world, then We will compel them, that is, We will force them, to a severe punishment, that is, terrible, difficult, and arduous for the souls, as God Almighty said, “Indeed, those who invent falsehood against God will not succeed. Enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment.” Because of what they used to disbelieve.

31:25: God Almighty says, informing us about these polytheists who associate others with Him, that they know that God is the Creator of the heavens and the earth alone, with no partner, and yet they worship partners with Him who acknowledge that they are His creation and His property. For this reason, God Almighty said: And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ They will surely say, ‘God.’ Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ That is, when the proof is established against you through your admission, But most of them do not know. Then God Almighty said: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, that is, He is His creation and His property. Indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, that is, the Free of need of anything other than Him. Everything is in need of Him, the Praiseworthy in all that He created. To Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth for what He created and legislated, and He is the Praised One in all matters.

31:27: The Almighty says, informing about His greatness, pride, majesty, beautiful names, sublime attributes, and His perfect words that no one can encompass, and no human being has knowledge of their essence and counting, as the Master of mankind and the Seal of the Messengers said, “I cannot count Your praises. You are as You have praised Yourself.” The Almighty said, And if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea were made ink, and seven more seas were made to replenish it, the Words of God would not be exhausted. That is, if all the trees on the earth were made pens, and the sea were made ink, and seven more seas were made to replenish it, and the Words of God were written with them, indicating His greatness, attributes, and majesty, the pens would be broken, and the water of the sea would be exhausted, even if the like of them came as replenishment. The seven were mentioned for the sake of exaggeration, and there was no limitation intended, nor was there seven existing seas surrounding the world, as is said by those who receive it from the Israelite traditions that are neither truthful nor false. Rather, as the Almighty said in the other verse, “Say, ‘If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted. And if We brought “With its like” is not meant to be another only, but rather with its like, then its like, then its like, then so on and so forth, because there is no limit to the verses and words of God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: If the trees of the earth were pens, and the sea were ink, and God said: Indeed, such and such is my affair, and such and such is my affair, the water of the sea would be exhausted and the pens would be broken. Qatada said: The polytheists said: These are words that are about to be exhausted, so God the Most High said: And if all the trees on the earth were pens, meaning, if the trees of the earth were pens, and the sea were seven seas, the wonders of my Lord, His wisdom, creation, and knowledge would not be exhausted. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: The knowledge of all of the servants compared to God’s knowledge is like a drop of water in all the seas. God revealed this verse: And if all the trees on the earth were pens, meaning, if the sea were ink for the words of God, and all the trees were pens, the pens would be broken, the water of the sea would be used up, and the words of God would remain unbroken, because no one can measure His value or praise Him as He should, until He is the One who praises Himself. Our Lord is as He says and above what we say. It has been narrated that this verse was revealed in response to the Jews. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “The Jewish rabbis said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina: ‘O Muhammad, tell me, when you say, “And of knowledge you have been given only a little,” do you mean us or your people?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Both of you.’ They said: ‘Do you not recite in what has come to you that we have been given the Torah, in which is an explanation of all things?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is little in the knowledge of God, and you have what is sufficient for you.’ And God revealed concerning what they asked Him about in this regard: ‘And if all the trees on the earth were pens…’” The verse was also narrated in this manner from Ikrimah and Ata’ ibn Bishr. This indicates that this verse was revealed in Medina, not Meccan, but the well-known view is that it was revealed in Mecca, and God knows best. And His statement, Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise, meaning that He is Exalted in Might and has subdued and overcome all things. So there is no one who can prevent what He wills, nor is there anyone who can oppose or question His judgment. He is Wise in His creation, command, words, actions, law, and all His affairs. And His statement, He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul, meaning that He did not create all people and resurrect them on the Day of Resurrection, in relation to His power, except as the creation of a single soul. Everything is easy for Him. His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, Be, and it is. "And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye," meaning that He does not command something except once, so that thing is and does not need to be repeated or emphasized. "It is but a single cry, and at once they are awake. And His statement, Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing," meaning that just as He hears their words and sees their actions, as His hearing and sight are in relation to a single soul, so too is His power over them as His power over a single soul. For this reason, the Most High said, "He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul," the verse.

31:29: God the Almighty says that He causes the night to enter the day meaning He takes from it the day, so that one becomes long and the other becomes short. This is during the summer, the day lengthens to an extreme, then it begins to decrease, so the night lengthens and the day shortens. This is during the winter. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course for a specified term It was said to a specific term, and it was said to the Day of Resurrection. Both meanings are correct. The first statement is supported by the hadith of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him in the two Sahihs, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: O Abu Dharr, do you know where this sun goes? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: "It goes and prostrates beneath the Throne, then it asks permission of its Lord, and it is about to be told: "Return from whence you came." Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Saleh told us, Yahya bin Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: The sun is like a waterwheel that runs in the sky during the day in its orbit, and when it sets, it runs at night in its orbit under the earth until it rises from its east. He said: And the same is true of the moon. Its chain of transmission is authentic. And His statement, "And that God is Acquainted with what you do, is like His statement, Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? The meaning of this is that He, the Most High, is the Creator who knows all things, as in His statement, God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof," (al-An'am 2:17). And His statement, "That is because God - He is the Truth, and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood," meaning, He only shows you His signs so that you may use them as evidence that He is the Truth, that is, the true existent, the true God, and that everything other than Him is false. He is independent of anything other than Him, and everything is in need of Him, because everything in the heavens and the earth is His creation and His servants. Not one of them is able to move an atom except by His permission. Even if all the people of the earth gathered together to create a fly, they would be unable to do so. For this reason, God, the Most High, said, "That is because God - He is the Truth, and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because God - He is the Most High, the Grand," meaning, the Most High than whom there is no higher, the Grand One who is greater than everything, so every submissive person is insignificant in comparison to Him.
31:30: God the Almighty says that He causes the night to enter the day meaning He takes from it the day, so that one becomes long and the other becomes short. This is during the summer, the day lengthens to an extreme, then it begins to decrease, so the night lengthens and the day shortens. This is during the winter. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course for a specified term It was said to a specific term, and it was said to the Day of Resurrection. Both meanings are correct. The first statement is supported by the hadith of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him in the two Sahihs, that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: O Abu Dharr, do you know where this sun goes? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: "It goes and prostrates beneath the Throne, then it asks permission of its Lord, and it is about to be told: "Return from whence you came." Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Saleh told us, Yahya bin Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: The sun is like a waterwheel that runs in the sky during the day in its orbit, and when it sets, it runs at night in its orbit under the earth until it rises from its east. He said: And the same is true of the moon. Its chain of transmission is authentic. And His statement, "And that God is Acquainted with what you do, is like His statement, Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? The meaning of this is that He, the Most High, is the Creator who knows all things, as in His statement, God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof," (al-An'am 2:17). And His statement, "That is because God - He is the Truth, and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood," meaning, He only shows you His signs so that you may use them as evidence that He is the Truth, that is, the true existent, the true God, and that everything other than Him is false. He is independent of anything other than Him, and everything is in need of Him, because everything in the heavens and the earth is His creation and His servants. Not one of them is able to move an atom except by His permission. Even if all the people of the earth gathered together to create a fly, they would be unable to do so. For this reason, God, the Most High, said, "That is because God - He is the Truth, and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because God - He is the Most High, the Grand," meaning, the Most High than whom there is no higher, the Grand One who is greater than everything, so every submissive person is insignificant in comparison to Him.
31:31: God Almighty tells us that He is the One who subjected the sea for ships to sail in by His command, that is, by His kindness and His subjugation. If it were not for the power He placed in the water to carry the ships, they would not have sailed. For this reason, He said, To show you some of His signs, that is, of His power. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful, that is, patient in adversity and grateful in prosperity. Then God Almighty said, And when waves cover them like canopies, that is, like mountains and clouds, they call upon God, devoting their religion to Him alone, just as God Almighty said, And when harm touches you at sea, lost are those you call upon except Him, and God Almighty said, Then when they embark on a ship, the verse. Then God the Almighty said: {But when He delivered them to land, some of them were moderate.} Mujahid said: That is, disbelievers. It is as if he interpreted the moderate here as the ungrateful, as God the Almighty said: {But when He delivered them to land, at once they associated others with God.} Ibn Zayd said: It is the moderate in action. This is what Ibn Zayd said is what is meant in the words of God the Almighty: {And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate.} The moderate here is the moderate in action. It is possible that it is meant here as well, and it is a form of denouncing the one who witnessed those horrors, great matters, and dazzling signs in the sea. Then, after God bestowed salvation upon him, he should have responded to that with perfect action, diligent worship, and hastened to do good deeds. So whoever was moderate after that was negligent, and this is the case, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: And none denies Our verses except every traitor and ungrateful person. The traitor is the treacherous person, as stated by Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Malik on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: He is the one who breaks his covenant every time he makes a promise. The treacherous person is the most complete and extreme form of treachery. Amr ibn Ma’dikarib said: If you had seen Abu Umair, you would have filled your hands with treachery and deceit. His saying ungrateful means he is ungrateful for blessings, does not thank them, but rather forgets them and does not remember them.
