31:33: God the Almighty says, warning the people of the Day of Resurrection, commanding them to fear Him, to be in awe of Him, and to dread the Day of Resurrection when no father can avail his son meaning if he wanted to ransom his son with himself, it would not be accepted from him. And likewise if a son wanted to ransom his father with himself, it would not be accepted from him. Then He returns to admonishing them by saying, So let not the worldly life deceive you meaning do not let the tranquility in it distract you from the Hereafter and do not let the Deceiver deceive you about God meaning Satan. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: “He deceives the son of Adam, makes promises to him and gives him false hope. But Satan does not promise them except delusion.” Wahb ibn Munabbih said: “Uzair, peace be upon him, said: When I saw the affliction of my people, my grief intensified, my worries increased and my sleep was disturbed. So I beseeched my Lord, prayed and fasted. While I was beseeching and weeping, the angel came to me and I said to him: ‘Tell me, do the souls of the believers intercede for the oppressors or the fathers for their sons?’” He said: The Day of Resurrection will be the final judgment, and there will be a kingdom that is apparent in which there is no permission, and no one will speak in it except by the permission of the Most Merciful. No father will be taken from his son, nor a son from his father, nor a brother from his brother, nor a slave from his master. No one will care for him except him, nor will anyone grieve for his grief, nor will anyone have mercy on him. Everyone will be compassionate for himself, and no one will be taken from another. Everyone will be concerned about his own concern, and will weep for his family, and will bear his burden, and no one will bear his burden with him except him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.
31:34: These are the keys of the unseen that God has kept to Himself, and no one knows them except after He has informed Him of them. Thus, no sent prophet or close angel knows the time of the Hour. None reveals its time except Him. Similarly, no one knows the sending down of rain except God, but when He commands it, the angels assigned to do so and whomever God wills of His creation know about it. Similarly, no one knows what is in the wombs of what God wants to create except Him, but when He commands it to be male or female, wretched or blessed, the angels assigned to do so and whomever God wills of His creation know about it. Similarly, no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow in this world or the hereafter. And no soul perceives in what land it will die, in its own country or any other of God’s countries. No one has any knowledge of that. This is similar to the words of God, the Most High, “And with Him are the keys of the unseen. None knows them except Him.” The Sunnah has mentioned that these five are called the keys of the unseen. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid bin Al-Hubab told us, Hussain bin Waqid told me, Abdullah bin Buraidah told me, I heard Abu Buraidah say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There are five things that no one knows except God, the Almighty and Majestic: God has knowledge of the Hour, sends down the rain, and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.” This is a hadith with a sound chain of transmission, but they did not include it. Hadith of Ibn Umar Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The keys of the unseen are five, and none knows them but God: ‘Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.’” Al-Bukhari was the only one to narrate it, as he narrated it in the Book of Istisqa’ in his Sahih on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf al-Firyabi on the authority of Sufyan bin Sa`id al-Thawri on his authority. And he narrated it in Tafsir from another chain of transmission, saying: Yahya bin Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Umar bin Muhammad bin Zaid bin Abdullah bin Umar narrated to me that his father narrated to him that Abdullah bin Umar said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The keys of the unseen are five. Then he recited: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. He is the only one who narrated it. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ghundar on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Umar bin Muhammad that he heard his father narrating on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I have been given the keys to everything except five: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.” Hadith of Ibn Masoud may God be pleased with him. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us from Shu’bah, Amr ibn Murrah narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Salamah who said: Abdullah said: “Your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was given the keys to everything except five: ‘Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.’” And this is how it was narrated from Muhammad ibn Ja’far from Shu’bah from Amr ibn Murrah with this chain of narration. And he added at the end of it. He said: I said to him, did you hear it from Abdullah? He said: Yes, more than fifty times. And he also narrated it from Wakee’ from Misa’ar from Amr ibn Murrah with this chain of narration. This chain of narration is hasan according to the criteria of the compilers of Sunan, but they did not include it. Hadith of Abu Hurairah Al-Bukhari said when interpreting this verse: Ishaq narrated to us from Jarir from Abu Hayyan from Abu Zur’ah from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, “One day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was present among the people when a man came to him walking and said: O Messenger of God, what is faith? He said: Faith is to believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the meeting with Him, and to believe in the afterlife. He said: O Messenger of God, what is Islam? He said: Islam is to worship God and not associate anything with Him, to establish prayer, to pay the obligatory zakat, and to fast Ramadan. He said: O Messenger of God, what is ihsan? He said: Ihsan is to worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. He said: O Messenger of God, when will the Hour be? He said: The one asked about it does not know more than the one asking, but I will tell you about its signs: When the slave girl gives birth to her mistress, that is one of its signs. And when the barefoot and naked people become the leaders of the people, that is one of its signs. There are five that no one knows but God: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down rain, and He knows what is in The wombs the verse, then the man turned away and said, “Bring him back to me.” They went to bring him back, but they did not see anything. He said, This was Gabriel who came to teach the people their religion. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in the Book of Faith, and Muslim through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Hayyan. We have already discussed it at the beginning of our commentary on Al-Bukhari, and we then mentioned the hadith of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn Al-Khattab, about this in full, and it is one of the individuals in Muslim. Hadith of Ibn Abbas Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Abdul Hamid told us, Shahr told us, Abdullah ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both told us, he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sat in a gathering, then Gabriel came to him and sat in front of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), placing his hands on the Prophet’s knees (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: O Messenger of God, tell me what Islam is? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Islam is that you submit your face to God, the Almighty, and bear witness that there is no god but Him alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He said: If you do that, then you have submitted to Islam? He said: If you do that, then you have submitted to Islam. He said: O Messenger of God, tell me what faith is? He said: Faith is that you believe in God, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, the prophets, and that you believe in death and life after death, and that you believe in Paradise and Hell, and the reckoning and the balance, and that you believe in all of destiny: its good and its bad. He said: If you do that, then you have believed. He said: O Messenger of God, tell me what…” Goodness? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Goodness is to work for God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, yet He sees you. He said: O Messenger of God, tell me when the Hour will be? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Glory be to God - in five things that no one knows except Him: Verily, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted. But if you wish, I will tell you of signs other than that.” He said: Yes, O Messenger of God, so tell me. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: When you see a slave girl giving birth to her mistress - or her master - and you see the owners of sheep competing in building tall buildings, and you see the barefoot, hungry, and destitute people being the leaders of the people, then that is from the signs and portents of the Hour. He said: O Messenger of God, and who are the barefoot, hungry, and destitute owners of sheep? He said: The Arabs.” A strange hadith, and they did not report it. Hadith of a man from Banu Amir Imam Ahmad narrated: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rib`i ibn Harash, on the authority of a man from Banu Amir, “He asked permission to see the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘May I enter?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a servant girl, ‘Go out to him, for he does not know how to ask permission.’ So tell him to say, ‘Peace be upon you. May I enter?’ I heard him say that, so I said, ‘Peace be upon you. May I enter?’ So he gave me permission, and I entered. I said, ‘What have you brought us?’ He said, ‘I have come to you with nothing but good. I have come to you so that you worship God alone, with no partner, and that you call upon Al-Lat and Al-`Uzza, and that you pray five times a day and night, and that you fast one month a year, and that you perform Hajj to the House, and that you take Zakat from the wealth of your rich and give it to your poor.’ He said, ‘Is there anything left of knowledge that you do not know?’ He said, ‘God Almighty has taught me good, and there is knowledge that no one knows except God Almighty: the fifth.’ ‘Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour.’ And He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs the verse. This is a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: A man from the desert came and said: My wife is pregnant, so tell me what she will give birth to. Our land is barren, so tell me when the rain will fall. I know when I gave birth, so tell me when I will die. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.” Mujahid said: These are the keys of the unseen about which God, the Almighty, said: “And with Him are the keys of the unseen. None knows them except Him.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Al-Sha’bi said on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: Whoever tells you that he knows what will happen tomorrow has lied. Then she recited: And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow. And the Almighty’s saying: And no soul perceives in what land it will die. Qatada said: These are things that God has kept to Himself, and He has not informed any close angel or sent prophet about them. Indeed, with God is knowledge of the Hour. No one among the people knows when the Hour will come, in what year, or in what month, or night or day. And He sends down the rain. No one knows when the rain will fall, night or day. And He knows what is in the wombs. No one knows what is in the wombs, whether male or female, red or black, or what it is. And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow. Good or evil. And you do not know, O son of Adam, when you will die. Perhaps you will die tomorrow, perhaps you will be afflicted tomorrow. And no soul perceives in what land it will die. That is, no one among the people knows where his resting place is on Earth, whether in the sea or on land, on a plain or a mountain. It was stated in the hadith: If God wills to take a servant in a land, He makes him need it. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his great dictionary in the Musnad of Usamah ibn Zayd: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu al-Malih, on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God does not cause the death of a servant in a land except that He makes him need it. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Dawud Al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Matar bin Akash, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If God decrees the death of a servant in a land, He makes him need it. And this is how Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in Al-Qadar from the hadith of Sufyan Al-Thawri, then he said: It is good and rare, and nothing is known of Matar from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, other than this hadith. Abu Dawud narrated it in Al-Marasil, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu al-Malih ibn Usamah, on the authority of Abu Uzza, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God wills to take the soul of a servant in a land, He makes him have a need for it. This Abu Uzza is Yasar ibn Ubaydullah, and it is said that he is Ibn Abd al-Hudhali. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ibrahim, who is Ibn Ulayyah, and he said: It is authentic. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Issam al-Isfahani told us, al-Mu’ammal ibn Ismail told us, Ubaydullah ibn Abi Hamid told us, on the authority of Abu al-Malih, on the authority of Abu Uzza al-Hudhali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God wills to take the soul of a servant in a land, He makes him have a need for it, so he does not cease until he has come to it. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.” Another hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Ahmad bin Thabit Al-Jahdari and Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Qat’i told us: Umar bin Ali told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If God wills to take a servant in a land, He makes him need it. Then Al-Bazzar said: We do not know of anyone who traces this hadith back to the Prophet except Umar bin Ali Al-Muqaddami. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Sulayman bin Abi Masih told me: Muhammad bin Al-Hakam recited to me on the authority of A’sha Hamdan: He did not take anything from what he had collected except embalming materials for the day after separation, along with rags. And other than the scent of sticks that light for him, and say that is from the provisions of the departing Do not grieve over anything, for every young man is bound to die on his own. Anyone who thinks that death will miss him is justified by foolishness. In whatever town his fate is, if he does not go to it willingly, he will be driven Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir, may God have mercy on him, mentioned it in the biography of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn al-Harith, who was the blind man of Hamdan. Al-Sha’bi was his sister’s husband, and he was also married to al-Sha’bi’s sister. He was one of those who sought knowledge and jurisprudence, then he turned to the art of poetry and became known for it. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Ahmad ibn Thabit and Umar ibn Shabbah, both on the authority of Umar ibn Ali, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “If the term of one of you is in a land that has given him a need, and he reaches the furthest point of his life, God Almighty will take him, and the earth will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:‘O Lord, this is what You have entrusted to me.’” Al-Tabarani said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu al-Malih, on the authority of Usamah, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God does not cause the death of a servant in a land except that He makes him have a need for it.’”
